questions.question: A primipara is 1 hour postpartum. The uterus is boggy and deviated to the right. What should the nurse do first?
choices: Massage the fundus and assess bladder distention
Administer a tocolytic medication for now as ordered
Start oxygen at 10 L/min via mask as ordered during care
Prepare the client for immediate surgery during care
questions.explanation: A boggy uterus suggests uterine atony; the nurse first massages the fundus and checks whether a full bladder is displacing the uterus.

questions.question: During the fourth stage of labor, which finding requires immediate nursing action?
choices: Mild afterpains during breastfeeding
Temperature of 37.4°C (99.3°F)
Saturated perineal pad in 15 minutes
Pulse rate of 58 beats/min in this client
questions.explanation: Heavy lochia with rapid pad saturation suggests postpartum hemorrhage and requires immediate intervention.

questions.question: A woman at 32 weeks’ gestation reports painless vaginal bleeding. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Assess fetal heart rate and place client on bed rest
Encourage client to ambulate during care in this client
Prepare for external cephalic version in this client
Perform a sterile vaginal examination right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Painless bleeding in late pregnancy suggests placenta previa; fetal status should be checked and vaginal examination avoided.

questions.question: A laboring client suddenly complains of severe abdominal pain and has fetal bradycardia. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
choices: Uterine rupture
False labor
Round ligament pain
Mild placental calcification
questions.explanation: Sudden pain with fetal distress in labor is a classic emergency sign of uterine rupture.

questions.question: Which finding is expected in a newborn during the first 24 hours after birth?
choices: Absent Moro reflex in this client
No urinary output right away
Persistent central cyanosis
Acrocyanosis of hands and feet
questions.explanation: Acrocyanosis is a common transitional finding in the first day of life; central cyanosis is abnormal.

questions.question: A newborn has a respiratory rate of 72/min with grunting and nasal flaring. What is the nurse’s priority action?
choices: Place newborn prone and recheck in 8 hours right away
give oral glucose water at this stage in this situation
Report the findings and give prompt respiratory support
Delay assessment until after feeding during assessment
questions.explanation: Tachypnea with grunting and flaring suggests respiratory distress and requires prompt evaluation and support.

questions.question: Which vaccine is routinely given at birth in the Philippines according to standard newborn care policies?
choices: Varicella and influenza vaccine
Measles and oral polio vaccine
BCG and hepatitis B vaccine
DPT and MMR vaccine
questions.explanation: Routine newborn immunization includes BCG and hepatitis B at birth in standard programs.

questions.question: A postpartum mother with rubella non-immunity asks when she can receive immunization. Which response by the nurse is best?
choices: You should receive it only after your next pregnancy in this situation during assessment
You should wait until baby is 1 year old during assessment as the next step at this time
You can receive the rubella vaccine before discharge if you are not pregnant again
You cannot receive it while breastfeeding at this time for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Rubella vaccine is given postpartum to non-immune mothers and is not contraindicated by breastfeeding.

questions.question: A client in active labor is receiving oxytocin infusion. Which finding requires the nurse to stop the infusion immediately?
choices: Cervix dilated to 5 cm during assessment as the next step
Maternal request for ice chips as the next step at this time
Contractions lasting 95 seconds occurring every 2 minutes
Fetal heart rate 140/min with moderate variability
questions.explanation: Tachysystole from oxytocin can reduce uteroplacental perfusion; prolonged frequent contractions require stopping the infusion.

questions.question: Which statement by a breastfeeding mother indicates correct understanding of effective latch-on?
choices: My baby should take in the nipple and much of areola
I should hear loud clicking sounds with each suck
My baby should suck only the nipple tip for now as ordered
Breastfeeding should be painless from the first second
questions.explanation: Effective latch includes the nipple and much of the areola; nipple-tip sucking leads to pain and poor milk transfer.

questions.question: A child with acute glomerulonephritis is admitted with periorbital edema and hypertension. Which intervention is most important?
choices: Provide a high-sodium snack
Maintain strict bed rest for two weeks in all cases
Monitor blood pressure and fluid status closely
Encourage unrestricted oral fluids
questions.explanation: Fluid overload and hypertension are key concerns in acute glomerulonephritis and require close monitoring.

questions.question: The nurse is teaching a mother about oral rehydration for a child with mild diarrhea. Which instruction is correct?
choices: Give small, regular sips of oral rehydration solution
Use plain water alone for replacement as ordered during care
Stop all feeding for 24 hours during care in this client
Offer only carbonated soft drinks in this client right away
questions.explanation: ORS should be given in small, frequent amounts to replace losses while feeding is generally continued.

questions.question: Which sign is the best indicator of severe dehydration in an infant?
choices: Moist oral mucosa
Sunken fontanel and lethargy
Capillary refill under 2 seconds
Tears when crying
questions.explanation: Sunken fontanel with lethargy points to significant dehydration in infants.

questions.question: A child with measles is hospitalized. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
choices: Institute airborne precautions and monitor for complications
give aspirin for fever control in this client right away
Encourage bright light exposure right away at this stage
Give live vaccine during the acute illness at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Measles requires airborne isolation and supportive monitoring; aspirin is avoided in children with viral illnesses.

questions.question: A pregnant client asks why iron supplementation is prescribed. Which explanation is best?
choices: It prevents all types of congenital anomalies in this client right away at this stage
It guarantees a larger birth weight right away at this stage in this situation
It will stop morning sickness at once at this stage in this situation during assessment
It helps prevent maternal anemia and supports increased red blood cell production
questions.explanation: Pregnancy increases iron requirements because of expanding maternal blood volume and fetal needs.

questions.question: Which finding in a client with severe preeclampsia should the nurse report immediately?
choices: Urinary frequency in the third trimester
Fetal movement felt after meals
Dependent ankle edema at the end of the day
Epigastric pain and visual disturbances
questions.explanation: Epigastric pain and visual changes suggest worsening severe preeclampsia and possible eclamptic complications.

questions.question: The nurse is caring for a client after amniotomy. Which assessment is the priority immediately after the procedure?
choices: Fetal heart rate
Maternal temperature
Pain score
Cervical dilation
questions.explanation: After membrane rupture, the immediate priority is fetal heart rate assessment because cord prolapse can occur.

questions.question: Which sign most strongly suggests placental separation during the third stage of labor?
choices: Fetal head crowning in this situation
Regular contractions every 10 minutes
Maternal complaint of thirst as the next step
A gush of blood with cord lengthening
questions.explanation: Placental separation is indicated by a gush of blood, fundal rise, and lengthening of the cord.

questions.question: A neonate born to a diabetic mother is jittery and weak. What should the nurse suspect first?
choices: Polycythemia crisis
Necrotizing enterocolitis
Hypercalcemia
Hypoglycemia
questions.explanation: Jitteriness and weakness soon after birth in an infant of a diabetic mother commonly indicate hypoglycemia.

questions.question: Which statement by the mother of a child with febrile seizure needs further teaching?
choices: I should place my child on the side during the seizure
I should keep objects away from my child
I should restrain my child tightly during the seizure
I should note how long the seizure lasts
questions.explanation: The child should not be restrained tightly during a seizure because it can cause injury.

questions.question: When teaching a postpartum client about lochia, which statement is correct?
choices: Lochia should gradually change from rubra to serosa to alba
Lochia remains bright red for six weeks for now as ordered
Large clots are expected every day as ordered during care
A foul odor is a normal sign of healing during care in this client
questions.explanation: Normal lochia progresses from rubra to serosa to alba; persistent bright red bleeding or foul odor is abnormal.

questions.question: The nurse is assessing fetal well-being during labor. Which finding is most reassuring?
choices: Persistent fetal bradycardia at 100/min for now as ordered during care
Late decelerations after each contraction as ordered during care
Baseline fetal heart rate of 140/min with moderate variability
Absent variability for 30 minutes in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: A normal baseline with moderate variability is a reassuring sign of adequate fetal oxygenation.

questions.question: A postpartum client reports calf pain and warmth. Which action should the nurse take first?
choices: Massage the affected calf as ordered during care in this client right away
Place client in Trendelenburg position during care in this client
Assess for signs of deep vein thrombosis and keep client on bed rest
Apply a heating pad and encourage walking right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Calf pain and warmth raise concern for DVT; massage and ambulation could dislodge a clot.

questions.question: Which instruction is best when teaching a mother how to prevent neonatal hypothermia at home?
choices: Bathe baby in cool water daily during care in this client right away
Leave the head uncovered indoors in this client right away at this stage
Place the crib near an open window for ventilation right away at this stage
Keep baby dry, clothed, and in skin-to-skin contact when appropriate
questions.explanation: Drying, covering, and skin-to-skin contact help maintain newborn temperature.

questions.question: A client at 38 weeks has blood pressure 160/110 mmHg and hyperreflexia. What medication is commonly prepared to prevent seizures?
choices: Magnesium sulfate
Oxytocin right away
Methylergometrine
Terbutaline
questions.explanation: Magnesium sulfate is used for seizure prophylaxis in severe preeclampsia.

questions.question: Which finding is the earliest sign of increased intracranial pressure in an infant with meningitis?
choices: Absent gag reflex
Decerebrate posturing
Fixed dilated pupils
Bulging fontanel
questions.explanation: A bulging fontanel is an early sign of increased intracranial pressure in infants.

questions.question: A child with nephrotic syndrome is admitted with generalized edema. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?
choices: Avoid all immunizations permanently
Measure daily weight and abdominal girth
Restrict protein completely during assessment
Encourage a high-sodium diet as the next step
questions.explanation: Daily weights and girth help monitor fluid retention in nephrotic syndrome.

questions.question: The best method to assess pain in a preverbal infant is to:
choices: Use a validated behavioral pain scale
Wait for the infant to verbalize discomfort
Rely only on heart rate
Ask the infant to rate pain from 0 to 10
questions.explanation: Behavioral pain scales are appropriate for preverbal infants.

questions.question: A gravida 2 para 1 client says her contractions are irregular and disappear with walking. The nurse should interpret this as:
choices: Precipitous labor
Second-stage labor
False labor
Transition phase
questions.explanation: False labor contractions are irregular and often subside with activity.

questions.question: Which play activity is most appropriate for a hospitalized toddler?
choices: Push-pull toys and simple blocks
Lengthy competitive team sports
Monopoly with complex rules
A 500-piece jigsaw puzzle
questions.explanation: Toddlers benefit from parallel play and simple manipulative toys suited to their developmental level.

questions.question: A 2-month-old infant should be expected to:
choices: Use two-word phrases
Walk with support
Stack four blocks
Smile responsively
questions.explanation: A social smile is expected by about 2 months.

questions.question: A 6-month-old infant is expected to:
choices: Ride a tricycle for now as ordered during care
Speak in complete sentences as ordered during care
Roll from back to abdomen and sit with support
Dress without help in this client right away
questions.explanation: Gross motor skills around 6 months include rolling and sitting with support.

questions.question: A 9-month-old infant typically:
choices: Plays peek-a-boo and may pull to stand
Writes simple words during care in this client
Ties shoelaces in this client right away
Hops on one foot right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Peek-a-boo and pulling to stand are expected around 9 months.

questions.question: A 12-month-old child is expected to:
choices: Use scissors safely during care
Understand fractions in this client
Read short sentences right away
Say one or two meaningful words
questions.explanation: By 12 months many infants say simple meaningful words.

questions.question: A 3-year-old child most likely:
choices: Drives a bicycle in traffic in this client
Uses short sentences and pedals a tricycle
Solves algebra problems at this stage in this situation
Has fully mature abstract reasoning
questions.explanation: Three-year-olds commonly speak in sentences and pedal a tricycle.

questions.question: Which advice is best after DPT-containing immunization in an infant?
choices: Expect no reaction at all right away at this stage
Stop feeding for 12 hours at this stage in this situation
Apply comfort measures and monitor for mild fever
Give aspirin routinely during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Mild fever or soreness can occur; aspirin is not routinely used in children.

questions.question: Which vaccine is generally withheld during pregnancy because it is live attenuated?
choices: Inactivated influenza vaccine
Hepatitis B vaccine
MMR vaccine
Tetanus toxoid
questions.explanation: Live attenuated vaccines like MMR are generally avoided during pregnancy.

questions.question: Which sign after immunization should prompt immediate medical evaluation?
choices: Low-grade fever in this situation during assessment
Brief fussiness during assessment as the next step
Difficulty breathing and facial swelling
Mild soreness at the injection site
questions.explanation: Difficulty breathing and facial swelling may indicate anaphylaxis.

questions.question: The nurse explains that exclusive breastfeeding is ideally recommended for the first:
choices: 6 months of life
2 weeks of life
12 months without any complementary feeding
24 months only if formula is avoided
questions.explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first 6 months.

questions.question: Which statement about colostrum is correct?
choices: It is a sign of breast infection as the next step at this time
It is nutritionally useless at this time for now as ordered
It should be discarded before mature milk appears for now as ordered
It is rich in antibodies and important for newborn protection
questions.explanation: Colostrum provides immunologic protection and valuable nutrition.

questions.question: A newborn’s bilirubin level is rising. Which intervention helps reduce physiologic jaundice?
choices: Applying talcum powder
Frequent feeding to promote stooling
Keeping the baby NPO
Exposing the baby to direct sunlight for hours
questions.explanation: Frequent feeding promotes bilirubin excretion through stooling.

questions.question: A child with croup has inspiratory stridor at rest. What is the nurse’s priority?
choices: Place child flat and restrain movement for now as ordered during care
Maintain airway and prepare for humidified oxygen or nebulized therapy
Inspect the throat aggressively with a tongue blade during care in this client
Encourage crying to clear secretions in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Stridor at rest indicates airway compromise; airway support is the priority.

questions.question: Which finding in a pregnant client suggests iron-deficiency anemia?
choices: Fatigue with low hemoglobin and microcytic indices
Polyuria and ketonuria during care in this client
Proteinuria and edema only in this client right away
Elevated hemoglobin with flushing right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Low hemoglobin and microcytosis point to iron-deficiency anemia.

questions.question: When monitoring a woman receiving magnesium sulfate, which assessment is the priority?
choices: Respiratory rate and deep tendon reflexes
Fundal height in this client right away
Visual acuity alone right away at this stage
Bowel sounds every 15 minutes at this stage
questions.explanation: Magnesium sulfate can depress respiration and reflexes, so these are priority assessments.

questions.question: Which statement by the mother of a child with asthma shows correct understanding of trigger control?
choices: I should stop all play permanently
I should use cough syrup instead of prescribed inhalers
I should give antibiotics for every wheeze
I should reduce exposure to smoke and known allergens
questions.explanation: Avoidance of smoke and other triggers helps prevent asthma exacerbations.

questions.question: A client in labor asks when to push. Which instruction is best?
choices: Begin strong pushing with every early contraction at 2 cm
Hold your breath continuously for 2 minutes at this stage in this situation
Push before labor starts to shorten the first stage in this situation
Push only when the cervix is fully dilated and you feel the urge
questions.explanation: Pushing before full dilation can cause cervical edema and maternal exhaustion.

questions.question: A child with congenital heart disease squats after exertion. The nurse interprets this behavior as:
choices: Evidence of hypoglycemia at this stage in this situation during assessment
A sign of normal play behavior only in this situation during assessment
A cue for prompt oral feeding during assessment as the next step
A way to increase systemic vascular resistance and improve oxygenation
questions.explanation: Squatting can improve oxygenation in cyanotic heart disease by increasing systemic vascular resistance.

questions.question: Which finding best indicates that a newborn is experiencing cold stress?
choices: Polyuria and weight gain in this situation during assessment
Marked hypertension during assessment as the next step
Warm flushed skin with bradycardia as the next step at this time
Mottling, hypoglycemia, and increased oxygen consumption
questions.explanation: Cold stress increases oxygen and glucose consumption and may cause mottling and hypoglycemia.

questions.question: The priority teaching for a mother of a child taking oral iron is to:
choices: Mix the iron with milk to improve absorption
Use a straw or dropper and expect dark stools
Stop the drug if stools darken at this time
Give it with antacids for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Iron can stain teeth and darken stools; a straw or dropper helps reduce staining.

questions.question: Which sign in a postpartum client suggests endometritis?
choices: Scant lochia alba on day 10 as the next step at this time
Foul-smelling lochia with uterine tenderness and fever
Pulse of 56 beats/min in a relaxed client for now as ordered
Mild breast fullness on day 3 as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Fever, foul lochia, and uterine tenderness suggest uterine infection.

questions.question: The nurse is caring for a woman in the latent phase of labor. Which nursing action best promotes coping?
choices: give clear explanations and encourage breathing and relaxation techniques
Limit all oral intake even if permitted for now as ordered during care
Withhold updates to avoid anxiety as ordered during care in this client
Insist on complete silence and isolation during care in this client right away
questions.explanation: Supportive coaching and explanations improve coping during early labor.

questions.question: Which finding in a school-age child requires further assessment for possible abuse?
choices: Injuries in different stages of healing with inconsistent history
A scraped knee after supervised play as ordered during care in this client
Fear of an injection before vaccination during care in this client
A single bruise over the shin in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Inconsistent explanations and injuries in various healing stages raise concern for abuse.

questions.question: A newborn receiving phototherapy should have which nursing intervention?
choices: Stopping feedings during therapy
Routine application of lotion before each session
Eye protection and frequent repositioning
Keeping the newborn tightly swaddled at all times
questions.explanation: Eye shields and repositioning are standard nursing care during phototherapy.

questions.question: Which food is most appropriate to recommend to a pregnant client who needs more folate?
choices: Dark green leafy vegetables
Carbonated beverages
Processed salty snacks
Hard candy at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Leafy greens are good sources of folate, which helps prevent neural tube defects.

questions.question: A mother asks when to seek help for her newborn’s jaundice at home. Which response is best?
choices: Wait one week before reporting yellow discoloration in this client right away at this stage
Jaundice is always normal and needs no follow-up right away at this stage in this situation
Offer plain water and continue observation only at this stage in this situation
Seek care if jaundice appears in the first 24 hours or baby is difficult to wake
questions.explanation: Early jaundice or lethargy can indicate pathologic jaundice and needs prompt evaluation.

questions.question: Which assessment finding suggests fetal distress during labor?
choices: Recurrent late decelerations
Accelerations with movement
Baseline fetal heart rate 135/min
Moderate baseline variability
questions.explanation: Late decelerations are a nonreassuring sign of uteroplacental insufficiency.

questions.question: A mother of a toddler asks how to manage temper tantrums. Which response is best?
choices: Punish child physically each time at this stage in this situation
Use consistent limits and protect child from injury during the tantrum
Give in to demands to stop the crying during assessment as the next step
Ignore all behavior including safety risks as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: Consistent limits and safety are appropriate for managing tantrums.

questions.question: A postpartum client with Rh-negative blood has delivered an Rh-positive infant. Which medication is expected?
choices: Oxytocin to prevent sensitization in this situation during assessment
Rho(D) immune globulin within the recommended postpartum period
Methylergometrine to prevent antibody formation as the next step
Vitamin K to protect mother from hemorrhage at this time
questions.explanation: Rho(D) immune globulin helps prevent maternal sensitization after birth of an Rh-positive infant.

questions.question: Which finding in a child with appendicitis suggests possible rupture?
choices: Pain limited to the umbilicus with playfulness during assessment
Increased appetite as the next step at this time for now
Mild nausea relieved by crackers at this time for now as ordered
Sudden relief of pain followed by rigid abdomen and fever
questions.explanation: A ruptured appendix may cause a temporary pain decrease followed by worsening peritonitis signs.

questions.question: Which statement by a pregnant client demonstrates understanding of danger signs to report?
choices: Morning sickness always means baby is unwell as the next step at this time
Leg cramps at night never matter at this time for now as ordered during care
I only need to report labor pains after the due date for now as ordered during care
I should report vaginal bleeding, severe headache, or decreased fetal movement
questions.explanation: Bleeding, severe headache, and decreased fetal movement are important danger signs to report.

questions.question: A public health nurse is planning care for a barangay with high rates of diarrhea among children. Which action is the best primary prevention measure?
choices: Promote safe water, sanitation, and handwashing practices
Conduct surgery missions twice a year for now as ordered
Refer all children with diarrhea to tertiary hospitals
Start antibiotics for all household members during care
questions.explanation: Primary prevention for diarrheal disease focuses on sanitation, safe water, and hygiene.

questions.question: Which indicator best measures the health status of mothers and infants in a community?
choices: Total road length in kilometers
Household television ownership
Maternal and infant mortality rates
Number of sari-sari stores in this client
questions.explanation: Maternal and infant mortality rates are sensitive indicators of community health and health service access.

questions.question: A nurse using the bag technique in community visits should do which action first upon entering the home?
choices: Ask the family to touch the sterile items
Select a clean, safe work area for the bag
Place used articles back into the clean section
Open all compartments immediately on the dining table
questions.explanation: The nurse first establishes a clean working area to protect equipment and prevent contamination.

questions.question: A family refuses immunization because of misinformation. Which nursing approach is best?
choices: Threaten them with legal punishment at once during care in this client
Argue until they agree in this client right away at this stage in this situation
Explore concerns respectfully and give accurate, understandable education
Document refusal without any further discussion at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Therapeutic, respectful education helps address vaccine hesitancy more effectively than confrontation.

questions.question: Which level of prevention does blood pressure screening at a community fair represent?
choices: Primordial prevention only
Primary prevention
Secondary prevention
Tertiary prevention
questions.explanation: Screening aims to detect disease early, which is secondary prevention.

questions.question: When calculating the target population for immunization, the most important community data include the number of:
choices: Telephones per household right away at this stage
Eligible infants and children in the catchment area
Registered voters only in this situation during assessment
Tricycles operating daily during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Planning immunization services requires an accurate count of eligible children.

questions.question: Which statement about directly observed treatment short-course (DOTS) for tuberculosis is correct?
choices: It eliminates the need for sputum monitoring at this stage
It helps ensure adherence and reduce treatment failure
It shortens treatment to three days during assessment
It is used only for noninfectious diseases as the next step
questions.explanation: DOTS improves adherence and outcomes in TB management.

questions.question: A nurse identifies that many households store water in uncovered containers. Which nursing diagnosis is most appropriate at the community level?
choices: Acute pain related to surgery in this situation during assessment
Readiness for enhanced family processes during assessment
Risk for increased vector-borne disease transmission
Ineffective coping of hospital staff at this time
questions.explanation: Uncovered water containers increase mosquito breeding and disease transmission risk.

questions.question: Which action by a public health nurse best demonstrates community participation?
choices: Using only hospital-based strategies during assessment as the next step
Writing the plan alone in the health center as the next step at this time
Starting activities without consulting the barangay at this time for now
Involving local leaders in planning and implementing health programs
questions.explanation: Community participation means people and leaders help plan and implement programs.

questions.question: During an outbreak investigation, what is the first step after verifying that a problem exists?
choices: Write the final report at once as the next step at this time
Establish a case definition and begin systematic data collection
Vaccinate every resident regardless of indication for now as ordered
Close all schools permanently as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: A case definition guides consistent identification and counting of cases.

questions.question: A family’s youngest child is underweight. Which home visit observation is most useful for planning nutrition teaching?
choices: The color of family curtains at this time for now as ordered
How many radios are in the house for now as ordered during care
The brand of detergent they buy as ordered during care in this client
What food is actually available and how meals are prepared
questions.explanation: Available food and meal practices directly affect nutritional teaching plans.

questions.question: Which statement best describes tertiary prevention in community health nursing?
choices: Policies that reduce risk-factor emergence for now as ordered
Activities aimed at limiting disability and restoring function
Measures that prevent disease occurrence during care in this client
Screening to identify disease early in this client right away
questions.explanation: Tertiary prevention focuses on rehabilitation and limiting disability.

questions.question: A woman asks where she can obtain modern family planning services. What is the nurse’s best response?
choices: Discourage any questions about reproductive health as ordered
Tell her family planning is only for married women during care
Advise her to rely on myths from neighbors in this client right away
give available options and refer per local service guidelines
questions.explanation: The nurse should give accurate, nonjudgmental information and an appropriate referral.

questions.question: Which type of family is composed of parents and their unmarried children living together?
choices: Nuclear family
Communal family
Blended family
Extended family
questions.explanation: A nuclear family consists of parents and their unmarried children.

questions.question: In a disaster-affected evacuation center, which nursing action has the highest priority during the initial phase?
choices: Schedule elective surgeries in this client right away at this stage
Ensure safe water, sanitation, and rapid health assessment
Start long-term livelihood seminars at once at this stage
Focus on annual performance reports in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: In the initial disaster phase, survival needs, sanitation, and rapid assessment are priorities.

questions.question: Which criterion best identifies a high-risk family needing priority home visits?
choices: Watching television nightly right away at this stage
Having painted walls at this stage in this situation
Presence of vulnerable members and poor access to care
Owning a motorcycle during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Families with vulnerable members and limited access to care should be prioritized.

questions.question: A nurse wants to determine whether malnutrition is concentrated in one sitio. Which activity is most helpful?
choices: Community diagnosis using local data and mapping
Buying additional hospital beds in this situation
Sending all children to a distant city during assessment
Discontinuing weighing sessions as the next step
questions.explanation: Community diagnosis and mapping help identify where problems are concentrated.

questions.question: Which example best illustrates primary prevention for dengue?
choices: Eliminating mosquito breeding sites
Providing physical therapy after stroke
Teaching wound care after surgery
Checking fasting blood sugar annually
questions.explanation: Source reduction prevents dengue before illness occurs.

questions.question: In the family coping index, the nurse primarily assesses the family’s:
choices: Ownership of luxury items during assessment as the next step
Ability to deal with health-related tasks and problems
Monthly entertainment budget at this time for now as ordered
Preference for television shows for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: The family coping index looks at how the family handles health-related responsibilities.

questions.question: Which activity is part of cold chain maintenance for vaccines?
choices: Keeping vaccines within recommended temperature range
Placing vaccines in the freezer door without monitoring
Storing vaccines on a sunny windowsill
Using expired vials to avoid waste
questions.explanation: Vaccine potency depends on maintaining proper cold chain temperature.

questions.question: When teaching oral rehydration in the community, the nurse should emphasize that ORS should be given:
choices: Only if there is fever at this time for now as ordered
In small regular amounts after each loose stool
Only when diarrhea has stopped as ordered during care
Instead of all feeding during care in this client
questions.explanation: Small frequent amounts of ORS help replace losses effectively.

questions.question: Which statement best describes herd immunity?
choices: When enough people are immune, disease spread is reduced in the community
Each person becomes immune by exposure to sunlight as ordered during care
A disease is eliminated after one clinic visit during care in this client
Only vaccinated health workers are protected in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: High levels of immunity reduce transmission and indirectly protect others.

questions.question: A barangay health survey shows rising teenage pregnancy. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Plan adolescent reproductive health education with community partners
Wait until rates double before acting during care in this client right away
Eliminate prenatal services in this client right away at this stage
Focus only on geriatric exercise classes right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Programs should respond to identified priority problems using relevant education and partnerships.

questions.question: Which is the best example of secondary prevention for cervical cancer?
choices: Installing mosquito nets during care in this client
Providing hospice care in this client right away
Screening eligible women per local guidelines
Building playgrounds at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Screening detects disease early and is secondary prevention.

questions.question: A nurse teaches a client with hypertension about adherence to maintenance drugs. This is primarily an example of:
choices: Environmental sanitation in this client right away
Primary prevention only right away at this stage
Health education to support disease control
Vector control in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Teaching adherence helps control an existing condition and prevent complications.

questions.question: Which information is most important when preparing a spot map during an outbreak?
choices: Color of each house roof right away at this stage in this situation
Names of all celebrities in the area at this stage in this situation
Favorite foods of residents in this situation during assessment
Location of each case by place of residence or exposure
questions.explanation: A spot map displays where cases are occurring to identify clustering.

questions.question: When prioritizing families for follow-up, which family should the nurse visit first?
choices: A teacher asking about diet trends
A couple requesting travel advice next month
A healthy adolescent needing sports clearance
A newborn with poor feeding and fever
questions.explanation: A febrile newborn with poor feeding is an urgent high-risk case.

questions.question: Which role of the public health nurse is demonstrated when she coordinates with schools and local officials for a deworming campaign?

Hypermagnesemia
questions.explanation: Trousseau sign indicates neuromuscular irritability associated with low calcium.

questions.question: A client with acute kidney injury has very low urine output. Which finding requires urgent reporting?
choices: Shortness of breath with crackles
Preference for warm blankets
Slight ankle itching as the next step
Mild thirst at this time for now
questions.explanation: Oliguria with crackles suggests fluid overload affecting the lungs.

questions.question: A client with ulcerative colitis is in an acute flare. Which diet is commonly appropriate?
choices: Low-residue diet as prescribed
Spicy fried foods
Large servings of raw vegetables
High-fiber bran with seeds
questions.explanation: A low-residue diet may reduce bowel irritation during a flare.

questions.question: A client with severe vomiting has metabolic alkalosis. Which assessment finding is expected?
choices: A fruity odor to the breath from ketones
Kussmaul respirations
Severe diarrhea as the main cause
Slow shallow breathing as compensation
questions.explanation: Metabolic alkalosis may lead to compensatory hypoventilation to retain carbon dioxide.

questions.question: A client says, “I hear voices telling me to hurt myself.” What is the nurse’s priority response?
choices: Encourage client to argue with the voices alone at this time
Tell client the voices are not real and walk away for now
Assess the content of hallucinations and ensure prompt safety
Ignore the statement unless family confirms it during care
questions.explanation: Command hallucinations require immediate safety assessment and intervention.

questions.question: Which communication technique is therapeutic when a depressed client says, “Nothing matters anymore”?
choices: Tell me more about what you are feeling right now
Others have it worse than you as ordered during care
Let us not talk about sad things during care in this client
You should not feel that way in this client right away
questions.explanation: Open-ended exploration encourages expression and conveys acceptance.

questions.question: A client with mania is pacing constantly and intruding on others. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?
choices: Reason at length during peak agitation as ordered during care
Set clear limits and give a low-stimulation environment
Offer caffeinated drinks to increase focus in this client
Encourage group games with many rules right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Clients with mania need limit setting and reduced stimulation.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of a no-suicide or safety plan?
choices: It is unnecessary once mood improves for one hour during care
It guarantees that client will not self-harm in this client
It is one part of broader suicide risk management and follow-up
It replaces ongoing assessment at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: A safety plan supports but does not replace full suicide risk assessment and management.

questions.question: A client with paranoid delusions states, “The staff are poisoning my food.” What is the best nursing response?
choices: I understand that you feel unsafe; let us look at ways to help you eat comfortably
That is ridiculous and impossible right away at this stage in this situation during assessment
You are correct, the kitchen is dangerous at this stage in this situation during assessment
If you do not eat, you will be punished in this situation during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: The nurse acknowledges feelings without validating the delusion and works toward practical support.

questions.question: Which behavior is most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder?
choices: Alternating periods of mania and depression right away at this stage
Hearing voices commenting on actions at this stage in this situation
Repetitive handwashing to reduce anxiety despite skin irritation
Sudden flashbacks after trauma only during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Compulsions are repetitive behaviors performed to reduce anxiety.

questions.question: A client taking lithium should be taught to report which sign immediately?
choices: Severe diarrhea, vomiting, and tremors
A desire to drink water on a hot day
Mild thirst after exercise during assessment
Occasional hunger before lunch as the next step
questions.explanation: GI upset and tremors may signal lithium toxicity and need prompt evaluation.

questions.question: The nurse is caring for a client in alcohol withdrawal. Which finding requires immediate intervention?
choices: Increased appetite in this situation during assessment
A request for quiet music during assessment
Mild fatigue as the next step at this time
Seizures or severe autonomic instability
questions.explanation: Alcohol withdrawal can progress to life-threatening seizures or delirium tremens.

questions.question: Which intervention is best for a client experiencing a panic attack?
choices: Stay with client, speak calmly, and reduce environmental stimuli
Discuss childhood conflicts in detail at once as the next step
Leave client alone to gain control at this time for now as ordered
Argue that there is nothing to fear for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: During panic, the nurse should remain calm, stay with the client, and reduce stimuli.

questions.question: Which statement by the nurse best promotes trust with a client diagnosed with borderline personality disorder?
choices: You can decide the rules for the whole unit as the next step at this time
I will keep secrets from the team if you ask at this time for now
I will be consistent with the plan and let you know what to expect
I will bend the rules whenever you are upset as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Consistency and clear boundaries help build trust and reduce splitting.

questions.question: A client with schizophrenia is withdrawn and neglecting hygiene. Which symptom type is this?
choices: Command hallucination
Negative symptom
Obsessive compulsion
Flight of ideas
questions.explanation: Avolition and poor self-care are negative symptoms of schizophrenia.

questions.question: Which action is most important when administering haloperidol IM to an agitated client?
choices: Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms and ensure safety
Offer grapefruit juice with dose as ordered during care
Encourage sunbathing immediately after the injection
Expect the drug to improve nutrition instantly
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics like haloperidol can cause extrapyramidal side effects that require monitoring.

questions.question: A client with post-traumatic stress disorder reports nightmares and hypervigilance. Which nursing approach is most helpful initially?
choices: Use confrontation to challenge fear responses as ordered during care
give a calm environment and encourage grounding and coping skills
Discourage all discussion of symptoms in this client right away
Force detailed retelling of trauma right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Early supportive care includes safety, grounding, and coping strategies.

questions.question: When working with a client who has anorexia nervosa, which nursing priority is most important?
choices: Praise extreme weight loss as self-control during care
Monitor nutritional status and physiologic stability
Allow unlimited exercise after meals right away at this stage
Ignore food rituals to avoid conflict at this stage
questions.explanation: Physiologic stability and nutrition are priority concerns in anorexia nervosa.

questions.question: A client says, “I just want to go to sleep and never wake up.” What is the nurse’s best first action?
choices: Change the subject to improve mood in this client
Assess directly for suicidal intent, plan, and means
Leave client alone to rest at this stage in this situation
Promise secrecy in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Direct suicide assessment is indicated when a client expresses hopeless or death-related thoughts.

questions.question: Which response is therapeutic when a grieving client cries and says, “I still cannot believe she is gone”?
choices: Do not cry because it upsets others
You need to move on now
This must be very painful for you
At least she lived a long life
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the client’s pain is therapeutic and supportive.

questions.question: A client with dementia becomes more confused in the evening. This is best described as:
choices: Neologism
Echolalia
Sundowning
Confabulation
questions.explanation: Worsening confusion later in the day is commonly called sundowning.

questions.question: Which intervention is appropriate for a client with bipolar disorder who is in the depressive phase?
choices: Use rapid speech to match energy level in this situation during assessment
Assess suicide risk and encourage structured activity as tolerated
Withhold antidepressant teaching entirely as the next step at this time
give multiple stimulating group activities all night at this time
questions.explanation: Depression in bipolar disorder requires suicide assessment and supportive activity.

questions.question: A client on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should be monitored for which serious condition?
choices: Serotonin syndrome if symptoms such as agitation and hyperreflexia occur
Diabetic ketoacidosis in all clients as the next step at this time for now
Tardive dyskinesia only within one dose at this time for now as ordered
Permanent hearing loss for now as ordered during care in this client right away
questions.explanation: Agitation, hyperreflexia, and autonomic changes may indicate serotonin syndrome.

questions.question: Which nursing action is best for a client who is socially anxious at a group session?
choices: Exclude client from all future groups as the next step
Tell client anxiety is imaginary at this time for now
Force the client to speak first to build confidence
Sit with client initially and offer gradual participation
questions.explanation: Gradual exposure and support help socially anxious clients participate.

questions.question: A client with delirium is attempting to climb out of bed. Which intervention is priority?
choices: Begin long-term psychoanalysis at this time for now as ordered during care in this client
Encourage client to walk alone for now as ordered during care in this client
give close observation and address possible causes such as hypoxia or infection
Keep lights off and room isolated during care in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Delirium is often due to an underlying medical cause and requires safety plus urgent evaluation.

questions.question: Which statement by a family member of a client with major depression indicates need for further teaching?
choices: I should encourage treatment adherence and follow-up
I should help reduce isolation when possible as ordered during care
I should take suicidal statements seriously during care
I should tell him to snap out of it if he wants to improve
questions.explanation: Minimizing depression is not therapeutic; support and treatment are important.

questions.question: A nurse observes a client repeatedly checking the lock for 30 minutes. The best initial response is:
choices: The door is fine, so your feelings do not matter as ordered
You are wasting everyone’s time during care in this client
Stop that at once or you will lose privileges in this client
What thoughts are making it hard to stop checking right now?
questions.explanation: Exploring the anxiety behind the behavior is more therapeutic than shaming.

questions.question: A client receiving electroconvulsive therapy should be told that the procedure is commonly used when:
choices: Severe depression does not respond adequately and rapid improvement is needed
Any client with insomnia asks for it in this client right away at this stage
A client only has a mild situational worry right away at this stage in this situation
A client wants help memorizing school facts at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: ECT is often used for severe, treatment-resistant, or urgent depressive illness.

questions.question: Which milieu principle is best for an inpatient psychiatric unit?
choices: Avoid all social interaction among clients in this client right away
Allow rules to change each hour right away at this stage in this situation
give a structured, safe environment with predictable expectations
Use humiliation to control behavior in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: A structured, safe, predictable milieu supports therapeutic behavior.

questions.question: A client with generalized anxiety disorder asks for help with persistent worry. Which skill should the nurse teach?
choices: Avoid sleep to reduce rumination right away at this stage
Drink more caffeine for alertness at this stage in this situation
Use relaxation breathing and schedule brief worry periods
Stop all exercise during assessment as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: Breathing and structured coping strategies can help manage anxiety.

questions.question: Which finding suggests neuroleptic malignant syndrome in a client taking antipsychotics?
choices: Craving sweets at bedtime at this stage in this situation during assessment
Mild dry mouth after one dose in this situation during assessment
Localized rash from adhesive tape during assessment as the next step
High fever, severe muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability
questions.explanation: NMS is a rare but life-threatening antipsychotic reaction.

questions.question: Which intervention is most appropriate for a client with autism spectrum disorder who becomes overstimulated?
choices: Reduce sensory input and use clear, simple communication
Add loud music to distract the client during assessment
Use sarcasm to gain attention as the next step at this time
Change directions every minute at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Reducing sensory overload and keeping communication simple are helpful.

questions.question: The nurse is leading an anger management session. Which statement reflects healthy coping?
choices: I can step away briefly and use breathing before I respond
I should threaten others so they listen as the next step
I should bottle up anger until it explodes at this time
I should hit a wall to release tension for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Time-out and controlled breathing are healthier anger management strategies.

questions.question: A client with substance use disorder says, “I can stop anytime.” This statement most likely reflects:
choices: Projection
Denial
Sublimation
Displacement
questions.explanation: Minimizing or refusing to recognize the problem is denial.

questions.question: Which intervention is therapeutic for a client hearing non-command auditory hallucinations?
choices: Present reality briefly and redirect to a concrete activity
Tell client to obey the voices to reduce stress for now
Leave client alone for long periods as ordered during care
Whisper with the staff about the behavior during care in this client
questions.explanation: Brief reality orientation and redirection can help clients cope with hallucinations.

questions.question: A client with dementia is searching for her deceased spouse. Which response is best?
choices: He died years ago, stop asking for now as ordered during care in this client
You are wrong, he will arrive at noon as ordered during care in this client
You miss him very much; let us sit together and look at your photo album
Why can you not remember anything? in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Validation of feelings and gentle redirection are preferred over harsh reality confrontation.

questions.question: A child with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is having trouble completing tasks. Which nursing suggestion is appropriate?
choices: Assign many long unstructured tasks as ordered during care
Expect sustained quiet sitting for hours during care in this client
Punish all movement at once in this client right away
Break tasks into short steps with clear, consistent cues
questions.explanation: Structured short tasks and consistent cues support attention and success.

questions.question: Which nursing action helps prevent splitting among staff when caring for a manipulative client?
choices: Allow each staff member to set different rules
Respond based only on personal preference in this client
Keep treatment plans secret from the team right away
Maintain consistent team communication and boundaries
questions.explanation: Consistent boundaries and communication reduce splitting behaviors.

questions.question: A client newly diagnosed with panic disorder asks what hyperventilation causes. Which explanation is correct?
choices: It always causes loss of consciousness in this client right away at this stage
It permanently damages memory after one episode right away at this stage
It raises blood glucose suddenly in every case at this stage in this situation
It can lower carbon dioxide levels and worsen dizziness or tingling
questions.explanation: Hyperventilation can reduce CO2 and cause lightheadedness and tingling.

questions.question: A client with depression who has just begun antidepressants says energy is returning. Why is close monitoring especially important now?
choices: client can now stop therapy right away at this stage in this situation
The medication always causes euphoria at once at this stage in this situation
Suicide risk can increase when energy improves before mood fully lifts
Nutrition is no longer important during assessment as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: Improved energy before mood recovery can increase ability to act on suicidal thoughts.

questions.question: Which behavior by a nurse best conveys genuine presence?
choices: Changing topics whenever emotions rise at this stage in this situation
Sitting quietly, listening attentively, and avoiding rushed interruptions
Checking the phone while client speaks during assessment as the next step
Arguing about every feeling as the next step at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Presence is communicated through focused, attentive, nonjudgmental listening.

questions.question: A client with conversion disorder suddenly cannot move one arm after severe stress. Which approach is best?
choices: Acknowledge the symptom and assess safety without accusing client of faking
Tell client the problem is imaginary during assessment as the next step
Force strenuous exercise at once as the next step at this time for now
Ignore the symptom completely at this time for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Symptoms should be taken seriously while maintaining a calm, nonjudgmental approach.

questions.question: Which statement about therapeutic boundaries is correct?
choices: Borrowing money from clients is acceptable if documented during assessment
Boundaries protect both client and nurse and support safe professional care
Sharing personal secrets is required for empathy at this time for now as ordered
Boundary crossings always improve trust for now as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: Professional boundaries maintain a safe therapeutic relationship.

questions.question: A client with delirium tremens is most likely to require which nursing priority?
choices: Long lectures on self-esteem as the next step at this time for now
Aromatherapy only at this time for now as ordered during care
Close monitoring of airway, vital signs, and severe agitation
Elective family counseling before hydration as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Delirium tremens is a medical emergency requiring close monitoring and supportive treatment.

questions.question: Which intervention is most helpful for a client with insomnia in an inpatient psychiatric setting?
choices: Keep bright lights on all night at this time for now as ordered
Offer caffeine after dinner for now as ordered during care in this client
Encourage consistent sleep hygiene and reduce evening stimulation
Schedule vigorous exercise at midnight during care in this client
questions.explanation: Sleep hygiene and a low-stimulation evening environment promote rest.

questions.question: A client says, “Everyone on the television is sending me messages.” This is best documented as:
choices: Euphoria for now
Flight of ideas
Confabulation
Ideas of reference
questions.explanation: Believing neutral events have special personal meaning is ideas of reference.

questions.question: A client with severe anxiety asks why he cannot think clearly. Which explanation is best?
choices: Anxiety proves psychosis is present as ordered during care
Thinking never changes during anxiety during care in this client
Anxiety permanently lowers intelligence in this client right away
High anxiety narrows attention and can impair problem-solving
questions.explanation: High anxiety reduces concentration and problem-solving ability.

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a client after a suicide attempt. Which intervention is essential?
choices: Allow privacy with all belongings at once during care in this client
Maintain close observation and remove access to harmful objects
Promise client there will be no more limits right away at this stage
Delay mental status assessment at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: After an attempt, safety through observation and environmental control is essential.

questions.question: Which action is most therapeutic when a client is escalating with anger?
choices: Use short, calm statements and allow personal space
Touch client without warning right away at this stage
Stand very close and argue loudly at this stage in this situation
Block the exit and stare in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Calm communication and adequate space reduce escalation risk.

questions.question: A client with schizophrenia is taking clozapine. Which laboratory monitoring is particularly important?
choices: Serum amylase only right away at this stage
Visual acuity monthly at this stage
Calcium levels only in this situation
White blood cell or neutrophil counts
questions.explanation: Clozapine can cause agranulocytosis, so blood count monitoring is important.

questions.question: Which response by the nurse is best when a client says, “I feel hopeless”?
choices: You should be grateful for what you have at this stage in this situation
Do not say that again in this situation during assessment as the next step
I am glad you told me; I want to understand more about that feeling
That is a weak attitude as the next step at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: The nurse should acknowledge disclosure and explore hopelessness further.

questions.question: A client with bulimia nervosa is at particular risk for which problem?
choices: Permanent blindness after vomiting in this situation
Electrolyte imbalance from purging behaviors
Progressive paralysis from one binge as the next step
Hypothermia from one skipped meal at this time
questions.explanation: Purging can lead to dangerous electrolyte disturbances.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects trauma-informed care?
choices: Use confrontation to test credibility during assessment as the next step at this time
Assume trauma may be present and prioritize safety, choice, and collaboration
Force disclosure to speed treatment at this time for now as ordered during care
Ignore triggers because they reinforce symptoms for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Trauma-informed care emphasizes safety, trust, choice, and collaboration.

questions.question: A manic client is refusing meals to continue talking and pacing. Which intervention is best?
choices: Withhold fluids until client sits quietly as the next step at this time
Offer high-calorie finger foods and fluids that can be taken on the move
Use food as a threat for now as ordered during care in this client right away
Require large formal meals at set tables only as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: High-calorie portable foods help maintain nutrition when the client cannot sit long.

questions.question: A nurse hears a client say, “If my pain does not stop, I may as well end it.” What is the nurse’s best action?
choices: Leave pain assessment for later at this time for now as ordered during care
Promise not to tell anyone for now as ordered during care in this client
Take the statement seriously and begin prompt suicide risk assessment
Assume it is only frustration during care in this client right away
questions.explanation: Any self-harm statement should be taken seriously and assessed promptly.

questions.question: A client with social withdrawal is making little eye contact. Which nurse behavior is best?
choices: Offer brief regular contacts without forcing interaction
Interpret the silence as defiance as ordered during care
Stop visiting until client talks during care in this client
Demand prolonged eye contact in this client right away
questions.explanation: Brief, consistent contact can build trust without overwhelming the client.

questions.question: Which statement about confidentiality is correct in psychiatric nursing?
choices: Confidentiality never has limits even with imminent danger as ordered during care in this client
All client information can be discussed with friends during care in this client right away
Information may be shared only with those involved in care or as required for safety or law
Family may always receive full details without consent right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is protected but may be limited by safety needs and legal requirements.

questions.question: A client with depression says food has no taste and refuses breakfast. Which nursing response is most helpful?
choices: Offer small regular meals and stay with client briefly while encouraging intake
Threaten tube feeding at once in this client right away at this stage in this situation
Tell client nutrition is not important today right away at this stage in this situation
Serve one very large meal only at this stage in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Small frequent meals and supportive presence often help depressed clients eat.

questions.question: Which intervention best supports reality orientation in early dementia?
choices: Use clocks, calendars, and simple repeated cues
Frequently rearrange the room right away at this stage
Provide multiple new caregivers every shift
Debate every mistaken statement in this situation
questions.explanation: Consistent cues such as clocks and calendars support orientation.

questions.question: Which response is most appropriate when a client asks the nurse for a personal social-media connection?
choices: Accept to improve rapport right away at this stage in this situation during assessment
Ask client to keep it secret at this stage in this situation during assessment
Ignore the question in this situation during assessment as the next step
Explain that professional boundaries prevent personal online relationships
questions.explanation: Maintaining professional boundaries includes avoiding personal online relationships.

questions.question: A client says, “People laugh at me everywhere I go.” Which nursing response is most therapeutic?
choices: No one is laughing at you, so stop worrying at this stage in this situation
Maybe they really are targeting you in this situation during assessment
You are too sensitive during assessment as the next step at this time
That sounds very distressing; can you tell me what happened today?
questions.explanation: The nurse explores the client’s perception and distress without dismissing or validating the belief.

questions.question: Which intervention is best when a client with dementia becomes agitated during bathing?
choices: Use multiple commands at once in this situation during assessment
Continue quickly despite escalating distress during assessment
Argue until client cooperates as the next step at this time
Simplify the task, speak calmly, and try again later if needed
questions.explanation: Simple calm communication and flexibility reduce agitation in dementia care.

questions.question: A client with severe depression remains in bed and speaks very little. Which nursing goal is realistic for the first day?
choices: client will show full remission by evening during assessment
The client will socialize with all peers for two hours
client will sit out of bed and interact briefly with nurse
client will lead a group session for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Early goals in severe depression should be small, realistic, and achievable.

questions.question: Which nursing intervention is most appropriate for a client with persecutory delusions?
choices: Avoid arguing about the delusion and focus on client’s safety and feelings
Ask other clients to convince client it is false at this time for now
Demand proof of delusion at once for now as ordered during care in this client
Agree completely with the delusion to build trust as ordered during care
questions.explanation: The nurse avoids reinforcing delusions while maintaining safety and addressing emotional needs.

categories.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When prioritizing care for several clients, which client should the nurse assess first?
choices: The client waiting for routine bedtime care
The client who wants a snack for now as ordered
client with compromised airway or breathing
The client asking for discharge papers during care
questions.explanation: Priority frameworks place airway and breathing problems first.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates informed consent?
choices: nurse signs for client when the unit is busy for now as ordered during care
A family member consents without regard to the competent client’s wishes as ordered
Consent is obtained after the procedure during care in this client right away at this stage
client receives sufficient information and voluntarily agrees before the procedure
questions.explanation: Informed consent requires adequate information and voluntary agreement before the procedure.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: The nurse notes a medication error has occurred. What is the priority action?
choices: Assess client first and report per policy
Wait to see whether symptoms develop
Change the documentation to avoid blame
Hide the error to protect the nurse’s job
questions.explanation: Client assessment and prompt reporting are priorities after a medication error.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which infection-control measure is most effective in preventing transmission in health care settings?
choices: Keeping all doors closed
Using perfume to cover odors
Wearing double gloves for every task
Hand hygiene at the right moments
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most important infection-control measure.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which nursing action is appropriate under standard precautions?
choices: Recap all needles with two hands in this client right away at this stage
Wear sterile gown for every blood pressure reading right away at this stage
Use gloves when contact with blood or body fluids is anticipated
Reuse single-use gloves when clean in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Gloves are used when exposure to blood or body fluids is anticipated.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A client refuses a prescribed treatment. Which principle should guide the nurse’s response?
choices: Ask another client to persuade them right away at this stage in this situation
Respect autonomy after ensuring client is informed and competent
Ignore the refusal and proceed in this situation during assessment
Force treatment because nurse knows best during assessment
questions.explanation: A competent client has the right to refuse after being informed.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement best describes negligence in nursing?
choices: Failure to act as a reasonably prudent nurse would in similar circumstances
Documenting care promptly in this situation during assessment as the next step
Maintaining confidentiality during assessment as the next step at this time
Following policy exactly as the next step at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Negligence is a breach of the standard of care causing harm.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Before delegating a task to nursing assistive personnel, the nurse must first consider:
choices: Whether the unit is noisy in this situation during assessment as the next step
Whether client likes the delegatee during assessment as the next step
Whether the task is stable, routine, and within the delegatee’s competence
Whether nurse feels tired at this time for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Safe delegation depends on the right task, client, circumstance, and competence.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action by the nurse best protects client confidentiality?
choices: Discuss client information only in private with those directly involved in care
Leave charts open in the hallway as the next step at this time for now as ordered
Share interesting cases on social media without names at this time for now as ordered
Answer questions from any curious visitor for now as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: Confidentiality requires limiting disclosure to appropriate people and settings.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When using aseptic technique for sterile dressing change, which action contaminates the field?
choices: Facing the field while working
Keeping sterile objects above waist level
Opening the first flap away from the body
Reaching across the sterile field
questions.explanation: Reaching across a sterile field contaminates it.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which documentation entry is most appropriate?
choices: Had a bad attitude during care at this time for now as ordered during care
Incision edges approximated, no drainage noted, client rates pain 3/10
Client is doing fine and looks good as ordered during care in this client
Seems much better than yesterday maybe during care in this client right away
questions.explanation: Documentation should be objective, specific, and measurable.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which vital sign finding in an adult should the nurse report promptly?
choices: Blood pressure 118/74 mmHg
Temperature of 36.8°C as ordered
Respiratory rate of 8 breaths/min
Pulse 78 beats/min in this client
questions.explanation: A respiratory rate of 8 indicates respiratory depression and requires prompt attention.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse is preparing to administer medication. Which of the following is one of the core rights of medication administration?
choices: Right patient
Right family visitor
Right hairstyle
Right room decor
questions.explanation: Medication safety includes verifying the right patient.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: What is the best method to prevent aspiration during oral feeding of a weak client?
choices: Feed the client while flat in bed
Offer large bites quickly in this client
Use a straw for all dysphagia cases
Position client upright and feed slowly
questions.explanation: Upright positioning and slow feeding reduce aspiration risk.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When obtaining a sterile specimen from a wound, the nurse should:
choices: Swab old dried exudate only in this client right away at this stage in this situation
Touch the swab to the bed linen right away at this stage in this situation
Cleanse the wound first as ordered and collect from viable tissue or drainage
Collect after applying topical ointment in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Specimens should be obtained from the wound area likely to yield useful organisms, not dried surface debris.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action best promotes safe body mechanics when moving a client?
choices: Bend from the waist with straight knees right away at this stage
Pull quickly with one arm at this stage in this situation during assessment
Use a wide base of support and keep the load close to the body
Twist the spine while lifting during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Good body mechanics protect both nurse and client from injury.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse witnesses another staff member diverting narcotics. What is the nurse’s ethical and professional obligation?
choices: Document it only in the nurse’s personal notebook
Ignore it unless a client complains
Report the concern through proper channels
Confront the staff member publicly in front of clients
questions.explanation: Professional accountability requires reporting suspected diversion through proper channels.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which finding should be charted immediately after a fall?
choices: Personal opinions about who is at fault in this situation
Only that an incident report was completed during assessment
Unverified assumptions about the cause as the next step
Client’s assessment, circumstances, and actions taken
