choices: Hoarse voice that improves with rest
Small amount of serosanguinous drainage
Stridor and respiratory difficulty
Mild incisional soreness
questions.explanation: Stridor may indicate airway obstruction and is a postoperative emergency.

questions.question: A client with peripheral arterial disease should be taught to:
choices: Avoid crossing legs and stop smoking
Elevate legs above the heart for long periods
Walk barefoot indoors for comfort
Apply direct heat to numb feet
questions.explanation: Smoking cessation and avoiding impaired circulation behaviors are important in arterial disease.

questions.question: Which action best prevents infection in a surgical wound?
choices: Remove drains with bare hands in this situation during assessment
Perform hand hygiene and maintain aseptic dressing changes
Reuse soiled dressing supplies as the next step at this time
Clean from the dirtiest area to the cleanest at this time
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene and aseptic technique are fundamental for preventing wound infection.

questions.question: A client with Cushing syndrome is likely to exhibit:
choices: Hyperglycemia and increased infection risk
Severe weight loss with hypotension only
Tetany and positive Chvostek sign at this time
Cold intolerance and constipation for now
questions.explanation: Excess cortisol can raise glucose and suppress immune response.

questions.question: Which assessment finding suggests improvement in a client treated for pneumonia?
choices: Rising respiratory rate and confusion
Increasing crackles with cyanosis
Decreased fever and easier breathing
New pleuritic pain and hemoptysis
questions.explanation: Clinical improvement in pneumonia includes reduced fever and better ventilation.

questions.question: A client with ileostomy requires teaching. Which statement is correct?
choices: The stoma should be scrubbed with alcohol daily at this time
The stoma should appear black for now as ordered during care
The pouch is unnecessary if output is small as ordered
Stool from an ileostomy is usually liquid to semi-liquid
questions.explanation: Ileostomy output is generally liquid or semi-liquid.

questions.question: A client with Addison disease is most at risk for:
choices: Hypotension and hyperkalemia
Severe hypernatremia
Marked hypertension from cortisol excess
Persistent tachycardia with hyperglycemia only
questions.explanation: Adrenal insufficiency can cause low blood pressure and high potassium.

questions.question: Which action is best when caring for a client with neutropenia?
choices: Limit oral hygiene as ordered during care in this client right away
Monitor for infection and use protective precautions as indicated
Take rectal temperatures routinely in this client right away at this stage
Serve raw fruits without washing right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Neutropenic clients need infection prevention and careful monitoring.

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a client receiving morphine IV. Which assessment is the priority before administration?
choices: Hair color during care in this client
Bowel pattern from last month in this client
Dominant hand right away at this stage
Respiratory rate and level of sedation
questions.explanation: Opioids can depress respiration, so respiratory assessment is critical.

questions.question: A client with glaucoma should be taught that the goal of treatment is to:
choices: Restore lost vision immediately in all cases
Whiten the sclera right away at this stage in this situation
Lower intraocular pressure and preserve vision
Reduce ear pressure in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Glaucoma treatment aims to lower intraocular pressure and slow vision loss.

questions.question: Which measure is most important to prevent falls in an older adult with confusion?
choices: Darken the room completely right away at this stage in this situation
Restrain client continuously at this stage in this situation
Raise all four side rails and leave unattended in this situation
Keep often used items within reach and give close supervision
questions.explanation: Environmental safety and supervision are effective fall-prevention measures.

questions.question: A client with a positive Trousseau sign most likely has:
choices: Hypermagnesemia
Polycythemia
Hypocalcemia
Hypernatremia
questions.explanation: Trousseau sign indicates neuromuscular irritability associated with low calcium.

questions.question: A client with acute kidney injury has very low urine output. Which finding requires urgent reporting?
choices: Mild thirst in this situation during assessment
Shortness of breath with crackles
Preference for warm blankets
Slight ankle itching at this time
questions.explanation: Oliguria with crackles suggests fluid overload affecting the lungs.

questions.question: A client with ulcerative colitis is in an acute flare. Which diet is commonly appropriate?
choices: High-fiber bran with seeds
Large servings of raw vegetables
Spicy fried foods
Low-residue diet as prescribed
questions.explanation: A low-residue diet may reduce bowel irritation during a flare.

questions.question: A client with severe vomiting has metabolic alkalosis. Which assessment finding is expected?
choices: Slow shallow breathing as compensation
Severe diarrhea as the main cause
A fruity odor to the breath from ketones
Kussmaul respirations
questions.explanation: Metabolic alkalosis may lead to compensatory hypoventilation to retain carbon dioxide.

questions.question: A client says, “I hear voices telling me to hurt myself.” What is the nurse’s priority response?
choices: Encourage client to argue with the voices alone at this time
Assess the content of hallucinations and ensure prompt safety
Ignore the statement unless family confirms it as ordered
Tell client the voices are not real and walk away during care
questions.explanation: Command hallucinations require immediate safety assessment and intervention.

questions.question: Which communication technique is therapeutic when a depressed client says, “Nothing matters anymore”?
choices: Let us not talk about sad things for now as ordered
You should not feel that way as ordered during care
Others have it worse than you during care in this client
Tell me more about what you are feeling right now
questions.explanation: Open-ended exploration encourages expression and conveys acceptance.

questions.question: A client with mania is pacing constantly and intruding on others. Which nursing intervention is best?
choices: Set clear limits and give a low-stimulation environment
Reason at length during peak agitation during care in this client
Encourage group games with many rules in this client right away
Offer caffeinated drinks to increase focus right away
questions.explanation: Clients with mania need limit setting and reduced stimulation.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of a no-suicide or safety plan?
choices: It is unnecessary once mood improves for one hour during care
It replaces ongoing assessment in this client right away at this stage
It guarantees that client will not self-harm right away at this stage
It is one part of broader suicide risk management and follow-up
questions.explanation: A safety plan supports but does not replace full suicide risk assessment and management.

questions.question: A client with paranoid delusions states, “The staff are poisoning my food.” What is the best nursing response?
choices: If you do not eat, you will be punished in this client right away at this stage in this situation
I understand that you feel unsafe; let us look at ways to help you eat comfortably
You are correct, the kitchen is dangerous at this stage in this situation during assessment
That is ridiculous and impossible in this situation during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: The nurse acknowledges feelings without validating the delusion and works toward practical support.

questions.question: Which behavior is most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder?
choices: Alternating periods of mania and depression right away at this stage
Sudden flashbacks after trauma only at this stage in this situation
Hearing voices commenting on actions in this situation during assessment
Repetitive handwashing to reduce anxiety despite skin irritation
questions.explanation: Compulsions are repetitive behaviors performed to reduce anxiety.

questions.question: A client taking lithium should be taught to report which sign immediately?
choices: Mild thirst after exercise at this stage
A desire to drink water on a hot day
Severe diarrhea, vomiting, and tremors
Occasional hunger before lunch as the next step
questions.explanation: GI upset and tremors may signal lithium toxicity and need prompt evaluation.

questions.question: The nurse is caring for a client in alcohol withdrawal. Which finding requires immediate intervention?
choices: Increased appetite in this situation during assessment
Seizures or severe autonomic instability
Mild fatigue as the next step at this time
A request for quiet music at this time
questions.explanation: Alcohol withdrawal can progress to life-threatening seizures or delirium tremens.

questions.question: Which intervention is best for a client experiencing a panic attack?
choices: Discuss childhood conflicts in detail at once during assessment
Leave client alone to gain control as the next step at this time
Stay with client, speak calmly, and reduce environmental stimuli
Argue that there is nothing to fear for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: During panic, the nurse should remain calm, stay with the client, and reduce stimuli.

questions.question: Which statement by the nurse best promotes trust with a client diagnosed with borderline personality disorder?
choices: I will keep secrets from the team if you ask as the next step at this time
You can decide the rules for the whole unit at this time for now
I will be consistent with the plan and let you know what to expect
I will bend the rules whenever you are upset as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Consistency and clear boundaries help build trust and reduce splitting.

questions.question: A client with schizophrenia is withdrawn and neglecting hygiene. Which symptom type is this?
choices: Command hallucination
Flight of ideas
Negative symptom
Obsessive compulsion
questions.explanation: Avolition and poor self-care are negative symptoms of schizophrenia.

questions.question: Which action is most important when administering haloperidol IM to an agitated client?
choices: Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms and ensure safety
Encourage sunbathing immediately after the injection
Offer grapefruit juice with dose during care in this client
Expect the drug to improve nutrition instantly
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics like haloperidol can cause extrapyramidal side effects that require monitoring.

questions.question: A client with post-traumatic stress disorder reports nightmares and hypervigilance. Which nursing approach is most helpful initially?
choices: Force detailed retelling of trauma right away as ordered during care
Use confrontation to challenge fear responses during care in this client
give a calm environment and encourage grounding and coping skills
Discourage all discussion of symptoms right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Early supportive care includes safety, grounding, and coping strategies.

questions.question: When working with a client who has anorexia nervosa, which nursing priority is most important?
choices: Allow unlimited exercise after meals during care in this client
Praise extreme weight loss as self-control in this client
Ignore food rituals to avoid conflict right away at this stage
Monitor nutritional status and physiologic stability
questions.explanation: Physiologic stability and nutrition are priority concerns in anorexia nervosa.

questions.question: A client says, “I just want to go to sleep and never wake up.” What is the nurse’s best first action?
choices: Assess directly for suicidal intent, plan, and means
Leave the client alone to rest right away at this stage
Change the subject to improve mood at this stage
Promise secrecy in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Direct suicide assessment is indicated when a client expresses hopeless or death-related thoughts.

questions.question: Which response is therapeutic when a grieving client cries and says, “I still cannot believe she is gone”?
choices: This must be very painful for you
You need to move on now
At least she lived a long life
Do not cry because it upsets others
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the client’s pain is therapeutic and supportive.

questions.question: A client with dementia becomes more confused in the evening. This is best described as:
choices: Sundowning
Neologism
Echolalia
Confabulation
questions.explanation: Worsening confusion later in the day is commonly called sundowning.

questions.question: Which intervention is appropriate for a client with bipolar disorder who is in the depressive phase?
choices: Use rapid speech to match energy level in this situation during assessment
Assess suicide risk and encourage structured activity as tolerated
give multiple stimulating group activities all night as the next step
Withhold antidepressant teaching entirely at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Depression in bipolar disorder requires suicide assessment and supportive activity.

questions.question: A client on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should be monitored for which serious condition?
choices: Tardive dyskinesia only within one dose during assessment as the next step
Permanent hearing loss as the next step at this time for now as ordered
Diabetic ketoacidosis in all clients at this time for now as ordered
Serotonin syndrome if symptoms such as agitation and hyperreflexia occur
questions.explanation: Agitation, hyperreflexia, and autonomic changes may indicate serotonin syndrome.

questions.question: Which nursing action is best for a client who is socially anxious at a group session?
choices: Force the client to speak first to build confidence
Sit with client initially and offer gradual participation
Tell the client anxiety is imaginary for now as ordered
Exclude client from all future groups as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Gradual exposure and support help socially anxious clients participate.

questions.question: A client with delirium is attempting to climb out of bed. Which intervention is priority?
choices: Begin long-term psychoanalysis at this time for now as ordered during care in this client
Keep lights off and room isolated for now as ordered during care in this client
give close observation and address possible causes such as hypoxia or infection
Encourage client to walk alone during care in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Delirium is often due to an underlying medical cause and requires safety plus urgent evaluation.

questions.question: Which statement by a family member of a client with major depression indicates need for further teaching?
choices: I should help reduce isolation when possible for now as ordered
I should encourage treatment adherence and follow-up
I should tell him to snap out of it if he wants to improve
I should take suicidal statements seriously in this client
questions.explanation: Minimizing depression is not therapeutic; support and treatment are important.

questions.question: A nurse observes a client repeatedly checking the lock for 30 minutes. The best initial response is:
choices: What thoughts are making it hard to stop checking right now?
Stop that at once or you will lose privileges during care
The door is fine, so your feelings do not matter in this client
You are wasting everyone’s time right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Exploring the anxiety behind the behavior is more therapeutic than shaming.

questions.question: A client receiving electroconvulsive therapy should be told that the procedure is commonly used when:
choices: Any client with insomnia asks for it during care in this client right away at this stage
Severe depression does not respond adequately and rapid improvement is needed
A client wants help memorizing school facts right away at this stage in this situation
A client only has a mild situational worry at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: ECT is often used for severe, treatment-resistant, or urgent depressive illness.

questions.question: Which milieu principle is best for an inpatient psychiatric unit?
choices: Avoid all social interaction among clients in this client right away
Allow rules to change each hour right away at this stage in this situation
give a structured, safe environment with predictable expectations
Use humiliation to control behavior in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: A structured, safe, predictable milieu supports therapeutic behavior.

questions.question: A client with generalized anxiety disorder asks for help with persistent worry. Which skill should the nurse teach?
choices: Avoid sleep to reduce rumination right away at this stage
Drink more caffeine for alertness at this stage in this situation
Use relaxation breathing and schedule brief worry periods
Stop all exercise during assessment as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: Breathing and structured coping strategies can help manage anxiety.

questions.question: Which finding suggests neuroleptic malignant syndrome in a client taking antipsychotics?
choices: Mild dry mouth after one dose at this stage in this situation
Localized rash from adhesive tape in this situation during assessment
Craving sweets at bedtime during assessment as the next step
High fever, severe muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability
questions.explanation: NMS is a rare but life-threatening antipsychotic reaction.

questions.question: Which intervention is best for a client with autism spectrum disorder who becomes overstimulated?
choices: Reduce sensory input and use clear, simple communication
Change directions every minute during assessment as the next step
Add loud music to distract the client as the next step
Use sarcasm to gain attention at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Reducing sensory overload and keeping communication simple are helpful.

questions.question: The nurse is leading an anger management session. Which statement reflects healthy coping?
choices: I should hit a wall to release tension during assessment
I should threaten others so they listen as the next step
I can step away briefly and use breathing before I respond
I should bottle up anger until it explodes for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Time-out and controlled breathing are healthier anger management strategies.

questions.question: A client with substance use disorder says, “I can stop anytime.” This statement most likely reflects:
choices: Displacement
Sublimation
Denial
Projection
questions.explanation: Minimizing or refusing to recognize the problem is denial.

questions.question: Which intervention is therapeutic for a client hearing non-command auditory hallucinations?
choices: Whisper with the staff about the behavior at this time for now
Present reality briefly and redirect to a concrete activity
Tell client to obey the voices to reduce stress as ordered
Leave client alone for long periods during care in this client
questions.explanation: Brief reality orientation and redirection can help clients cope with hallucinations.

questions.question: A client with dementia is searching for her deceased spouse. Which response is best?
choices: You are wrong, he will arrive at noon for now as ordered during care in this client
Why can you not remember anything? as ordered during care in this client
You miss him very much; let us sit together and look at your photo album
He died years ago, stop asking in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Validation of feelings and gentle redirection are preferred over harsh reality confrontation.

questions.question: A child with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is having trouble completing tasks. Which nursing suggestion is appropriate?
choices: Punish all movement immediately as ordered during care
Break tasks into short steps with clear, consistent cues
Expect sustained quiet sitting for hours in this client
Assign many long unstructured tasks right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Structured short tasks and consistent cues support attention and success.

questions.question: Which nursing action helps prevent splitting among staff when caring for a manipulative client?
choices: Keep treatment plans secret from the team during care
Allow each staff member to set different rules
Maintain consistent team communication and boundaries
Respond based only on personal preference at this stage
questions.explanation: Consistent boundaries and communication reduce splitting behaviors.

questions.question: A client newly diagnosed with panic disorder asks what hyperventilation causes. Which explanation is correct?
choices: It can lower carbon dioxide levels and worsen dizziness or tingling
It always causes loss of consciousness right away at this stage in this situation
It raises blood glucose suddenly in every case at this stage in this situation
It permanently damages memory after one episode in this situation
questions.explanation: Hyperventilation can reduce CO2 and cause lightheadedness and tingling.

questions.question: A client with depression who has just begun antidepressants says energy is returning. Why is close monitoring especially important now?
choices: client can now stop therapy right away at this stage in this situation
The medication always causes euphoria at once at this stage in this situation
Nutrition is no longer important in this situation during assessment
Suicide risk can increase when energy improves before mood fully lifts
questions.explanation: Improved energy before mood recovery can increase ability to act on suicidal thoughts.

questions.question: Which behavior by a nurse best conveys genuine presence?
choices: Checking the phone while client speaks at this stage in this situation
Changing topics whenever emotions rise in this situation during assessment
Arguing about every feeling during assessment as the next step at this time
Sitting quietly, listening attentively, and avoiding rushed interruptions
questions.explanation: Presence is communicated through focused, attentive, nonjudgmental listening.

questions.question: A client with conversion disorder suddenly cannot move one arm after severe stress. Which approach is best?
choices: Force strenuous exercise at once in this situation during assessment
Tell client the problem is imaginary during assessment as the next step
Ignore the symptom completely as the next step at this time for now as ordered
Acknowledge the symptom and assess safety without accusing client of faking
questions.explanation: Symptoms should be taken seriously while maintaining a calm, nonjudgmental approach.

questions.question: Which statement about therapeutic boundaries is correct?
choices: Sharing personal secrets is required for empathy during assessment as the next step
Boundaries protect both client and nurse and support safe professional care
Borrowing money from clients is acceptable if documented at this time for now
Boundary crossings always improve trust for now as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: Professional boundaries maintain a safe therapeutic relationship.

questions.question: A client with delirium tremens is most likely to require which nursing priority?
choices: Close monitoring of airway, vital signs, and severe agitation
Aromatherapy only at this time for now as ordered during care
Long lectures on self-esteem for now as ordered during care
Elective family counseling before hydration as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Delirium tremens is a medical emergency requiring close monitoring and supportive treatment.

questions.question: Which intervention is most helpful for a client with insomnia in an inpatient psychiatric setting?
choices: Keep bright lights on all night at this time for now as ordered
Encourage consistent sleep hygiene and reduce evening stimulation
Offer caffeine after dinner as ordered during care in this client
Schedule vigorous exercise at midnight during care in this client
questions.explanation: Sleep hygiene and a low-stimulation evening environment promote rest.

questions.question: A client says, “Everyone on the television is sending me messages.” This is best documented as:
choices: Flight of ideas
Ideas of reference
Euphoria during care
Confabulation
questions.explanation: Believing neutral events have special personal meaning is ideas of reference.

questions.question: A client with severe anxiety asks why he cannot think clearly. Which explanation is best?
choices: High anxiety narrows attention and can impair problem-solving
Anxiety permanently lowers intelligence during care in this client
Thinking never changes during anxiety in this client right away
Anxiety proves psychosis is present right away at this stage
questions.explanation: High anxiety reduces concentration and problem-solving ability.

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a client after a suicide attempt. Which intervention is essential?
choices: Delay mental status assessment during care in this client right away
Maintain close observation and remove access to harmful objects
Promise client there will be no more limits right away at this stage
Allow privacy with all belongings at once at this stage
questions.explanation: After an attempt, safety through observation and environmental control is essential.

questions.question: Which action is most therapeutic when a client is escalating with anger?
choices: Block the exit and stare in this client right away
Stand very close and argue loudly right away at this stage
Touch client without warning at this stage in this situation
Use short, calm statements and allow personal space
questions.explanation: Calm communication and adequate space reduce escalation risk.

questions.question: A client with schizophrenia is taking clozapine. Which laboratory monitoring is particularly important?
choices: Calcium levels only right away at this stage
Serum amylase only at this stage in this situation
Visual acuity monthly in this situation
White blood cell or neutrophil counts
questions.explanation: Clozapine can cause agranulocytosis, so blood count monitoring is important.

questions.question: Which response by the nurse is best when a client says, “I feel hopeless”?
choices: You should be grateful for what you have at this stage in this situation
Do not say that again in this situation during assessment as the next step
I am glad you told me; I want to understand more about that feeling
That is a weak attitude as the next step at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: The nurse should acknowledge disclosure and explore hopelessness further.

questions.question: A client with bulimia nervosa is at particular risk for which problem?
choices: Hypothermia from one skipped meal in this situation
Electrolyte imbalance from purging behaviors
Progressive paralysis from one binge as the next step
Permanent blindness after vomiting at this time
questions.explanation: Purging can lead to dangerous electrolyte disturbances.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects trauma-informed care?
choices: Ignore triggers because they reinforce symptoms during assessment as the next step
Force disclosure to speed treatment as the next step at this time for now as ordered
Use confrontation to test credibility at this time for now as ordered during care
Assume trauma may be present and prioritize safety, choice, and collaboration
questions.explanation: Trauma-informed care emphasizes safety, trust, choice, and collaboration.

questions.question: A manic client is refusing meals to continue talking and pacing. Which intervention is best?
choices: Require large formal meals at set tables only as the next step at this time
Offer high-calorie finger foods and fluids that can be taken on the move
Withhold fluids until client sits quietly for now as ordered during care
Use food as a threat as ordered during care in this client right away
questions.explanation: High-calorie portable foods help maintain nutrition when the client cannot sit long.

questions.question: A nurse hears a client say, “If my pain does not stop, I may as well end it.” What is the nurse’s best action?
choices: Assume it is only frustration at this time for now as ordered during care
Take the statement seriously and begin prompt suicide risk assessment
Leave pain assessment for later as ordered during care in this client
Promise not to tell anyone during care in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Any self-harm statement should be taken seriously and assessed promptly.

questions.question: A client with social withdrawal is making little eye contact. Which nurse behavior is best?
choices: Interpret the silence as defiance for now as ordered during care
Demand prolonged eye contact as ordered during care in this client
Offer brief regular contacts without forcing interaction
Stop visiting until client talks in this client right away
questions.explanation: Brief, consistent contact can build trust without overwhelming the client.

questions.question: Which statement about confidentiality is correct in psychiatric nursing?
choices: All client information can be discussed with friends as ordered during care in this client
Family may always receive full details without consent during care in this client right away
Information may be shared only with those involved in care or as required for safety or law
Confidentiality never has limits even with imminent danger right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is protected but may be limited by safety needs and legal requirements.

questions.question: A client with depression says food has no taste and refuses breakfast. Which nursing response is most helpful?
choices: Threaten tube feeding at once during care in this client right away at this stage
Offer small regular meals and stay with client briefly while encouraging intake
Tell client nutrition is not important today right away at this stage in this situation
Serve one very large meal only at this stage in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Small frequent meals and supportive presence often help depressed clients eat.

questions.question: Which intervention best supports reality orientation in early dementia?
choices: Use clocks, calendars, and simple repeated cues
Debate every mistaken statement right away at this stage
Frequently rearrange the room at this stage
Provide multiple new caregivers every shift
questions.explanation: Consistent cues such as clocks and calendars support orientation.

questions.question: Which response is best when a client asks the nurse for a personal social-media connection?
choices: Ask client to keep it secret right away at this stage in this situation
Explain that professional boundaries prevent personal online relationships
Ignore the question in this situation during assessment as the next step
Accept to improve rapport during assessment as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: Maintaining professional boundaries includes avoiding personal online relationships.

questions.question: A client says, “People laugh at me everywhere I go.” Which nursing response is most therapeutic?
choices: No one is laughing at you, so stop worrying at this stage in this situation
You are too sensitive in this situation during assessment as the next step
That sounds very distressing; can you tell me what happened today?
Maybe they really are targeting you as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: The nurse explores the client’s perception and distress without dismissing or validating the belief.

questions.question: Which intervention is best when a client with dementia becomes agitated during bathing?
choices: Continue quickly despite escalating distress in this situation
Simplify the task, speak calmly, and try again later if needed
Use multiple commands at once as the next step at this time
Argue until client cooperates at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Simple calm communication and flexibility reduce agitation in dementia care.

questions.question: A client with severe depression remains in bed and speaks very little. Which nursing goal is realistic for the first day?
choices: client will sit out of bed and interact briefly with nurse
client will lead a group session as the next step at this time
client will show full remission by evening at this time
The client will socialize with all peers for two hours
questions.explanation: Early goals in severe depression should be small, realistic, and achievable.

questions.question: Which nursing intervention is best for a client with persecutory delusions?
choices: Ask other clients to convince client it is false as the next step at this time
Avoid arguing about the delusion and focus on client’s safety and feelings
Agree completely with the delusion to build trust for now as ordered during care
Demand proof of delusion at once as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: The nurse avoids reinforcing delusions while maintaining safety and addressing emotional needs.

categories.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When prioritizing care for several clients, which client should the nurse assess first?
choices: The client asking for discharge papers at this time
The client who wants a snack for now as ordered
client with compromised airway or breathing
The client waiting for routine bedtime care
questions.explanation: Priority frameworks place airway and breathing problems first.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates informed consent?
choices: nurse signs for client when the unit is busy for now as ordered during care
client receives sufficient information and voluntarily agrees before the procedure
Consent is obtained after the procedure during care in this client right away at this stage
A family member consents without regard to the competent client’s wishes in this client
questions.explanation: Informed consent requires adequate information and voluntary agreement before the procedure.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: The nurse notes a medication error has occurred. What is the priority action?
choices: Change the documentation to avoid blame
Assess client first and report per policy
Wait to see whether symptoms develop
Hide the error to protect the nurse’s job
questions.explanation: Client assessment and prompt reporting are priorities after a medication error.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which infection-control measure is most effective in preventing transmission in health care settings?
choices: Keeping all doors closed
Hand hygiene at the right moments
Wearing double gloves for every task
Using perfume to cover odors
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most important infection-control measure.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which nursing action is appropriate under standard precautions?
choices: Use gloves when contact with blood or body fluids is anticipated
Wear sterile gown for every blood pressure reading right away at this stage
Recap all needles with two hands at this stage in this situation
Reuse single-use gloves when clean in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Gloves are used when exposure to blood or body fluids is anticipated.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A client refuses a prescribed treatment. Which principle should guide the nurse’s response?
choices: Ask another client to persuade them right away at this stage in this situation
Force treatment because nurse knows best at this stage in this situation
Ignore the refusal and proceed in this situation during assessment
Respect autonomy after ensuring client is informed and competent
questions.explanation: A competent client has the right to refuse after being informed.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement best describes negligence in nursing?
choices: Failure to act as a reasonably prudent nurse would in similar circumstances
Maintaining confidentiality in this situation during assessment as the next step
Following policy exactly during assessment as the next step at this time for now
Documenting care promptly as the next step at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Negligence is a breach of the standard of care causing harm.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Before delegating a task to nursing assistive personnel, the nurse must first consider:
choices: Whether the task is stable, routine, and within the delegatee’s competence
Whether the unit is noisy during assessment as the next step at this time
Whether nurse feels tired as the next step at this time for now as ordered
Whether client likes the delegatee at this time for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Safe delegation depends on the right task, client, circumstance, and competence.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action by the nurse best protects client confidentiality?
choices: Share interesting cases on social media without names during assessment as the next step
Leave charts open in the hallway as the next step at this time for now as ordered
Answer questions from any curious visitor at this time for now as ordered during care
Discuss client information only in private with those directly involved in care
questions.explanation: Confidentiality requires limiting disclosure to appropriate people and settings.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When using aseptic technique for sterile dressing change, which action contaminates the field?
choices: Reaching across the sterile field
Keeping sterile objects above waist level
Facing the field while working
Opening the first flap away from the body
questions.explanation: Reaching across a sterile field contaminates it.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which documentation entry is best?
choices: Had a bad attitude during care at this time for now as ordered during care
Seems much better than yesterday maybe for now as ordered during care
Incision edges approximated, no drainage noted, client rates pain 3/10
Client is doing fine and looks good during care in this client right away
questions.explanation: Documentation should be objective, specific, and measurable.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which vital sign finding in an adult should the nurse report promptly?
choices: Temperature of 36.8°C for now as ordered
Pulse 78 beats/min as ordered during care
Blood pressure 118/74 mmHg
Respiratory rate of 8 breaths/min
questions.explanation: A respiratory rate of 8 indicates respiratory depression and requires prompt attention.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse is preparing to administer medication. Which of the following is one of the core rights of medication administration?
choices: Right patient
Right family visitor
Right hairstyle
Right room decor
questions.explanation: Medication safety includes verifying the right patient.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: What is the best method to prevent aspiration during oral feeding of a weak client?
choices: Offer large bites quickly during care
Use a straw for all dysphagia cases
Position client upright and feed slowly
Feed the client while flat in bed
questions.explanation: Upright positioning and slow feeding reduce aspiration risk.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When obtaining a sterile specimen from a wound, the nurse should:
choices: Collect after applying topical ointment in this client right away at this stage
Touch the swab to the bed linen right away at this stage in this situation
Cleanse the wound first as ordered and collect from viable tissue or drainage
Swab old dried exudate only in this situation during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Specimens should be obtained from the wound area likely to yield useful organisms, not dried surface debris.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action best promotes safe body mechanics when moving a client?
choices: Use a wide base of support and keep the load close to the body
Pull quickly with one arm at this stage in this situation during assessment
Twist the spine while lifting in this situation during assessment
Bend from the waist with straight knees during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Good body mechanics protect both nurse and client from injury.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse witnesses another staff member diverting narcotics. What is the nurse’s ethical and professional obligation?
choices: Ignore it unless a client complains
Confront the staff member publicly in front of clients
Report the concern through proper channels
Document it only in the nurse’s personal notebook
questions.explanation: Professional accountability requires reporting suspected diversion through proper channels.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which finding should be charted immediately after a fall?
choices: Client’s assessment, circumstances, and actions taken
Personal opinions about who is at fault during assessment
Unverified assumptions about the cause as the next step
Only that an incident report was completed at this time
questions.explanation: The chart should contain objective assessment data, circumstances, and interventions.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A client is on contact precautions. Which equipment practice is correct?
choices: Place soiled linen on the floor during assessment as the next step at this time
Allow visitors to ignore hand hygiene as the next step at this time
Use dedicated equipment when possible and clean shared items properly
Carry used gloves in a pocket for reuse for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Dedicated or properly disinfected equipment helps prevent transmission.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement reflects beneficence?
choices: Doing whatever is easiest for staff
Acting to promote the client’s well-being
Keeping silent about unsafe care
Treating all clients exactly the same regardless of need
questions.explanation: Beneficence means acting for the good of the client.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which client statement shows correct understanding of advance directives?
choices: They replace my need to discuss values with my family at this time for now
They are written by nurses without my input for now as ordered during care
They are used only for financial decisions as ordered during care in this client
These documents express my health care wishes if I cannot speak for myself
questions.explanation: Advance directives state the client’s preferences for future health care decisions.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse is preparing to insert a urinary catheter. The most important action to prevent infection is to:
choices: Maintain sterile technique throughout insertion
Place the drainage bag above bladder level
Disconnect the closed system each shift
Use clean gloves only and touch the sterile catheter freely
questions.explanation: Sterile insertion and maintaining a closed system reduce catheter-associated infection.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which principle should guide time management for a beginning nurse?
choices: Document only at the end of shift as ordered during care in this client
Prioritize important and urgent care before less critical tasks
Avoid asking for help under any condition in this client right away
Complete easy tasks first regardless of urgency right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Safe time management begins with prioritization of urgent and important care.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A client with limited English proficiency needs teaching before surgery. Which action is best?
choices: Skip the teaching because the surgery is routine
Ask a young child to translate complex information
Rely on gestures only
Use a qualified interpreter
questions.explanation: Qualified interpreters help ensure accurate, ethical communication.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement about pain is correct?
choices: Nurses can judge pain accurately by facial expression alone
Pain is whatever the experiencing person says it is
Chronic pain is never real without visible injury
Vital signs always reflect pain intensity exactly
questions.explanation: Pain is subjective and should be assessed using the client’s report and other data.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates nonmaleficence?
choices: Sharing a client story for entertainment right away at this stage in this situation
Performing a task beyond competence at this stage in this situation during assessment
Skipping double-checks to save time in this situation during assessment as the next step
Checking client identity carefully before medication administration to avoid harm
questions.explanation: Nonmaleficence means avoiding harm through safe practice.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which type of isolation is indicated for suspected pulmonary tuberculosis?
choices: Droplet precautions only
Protective isolation only
Airborne precautions
Contact precautions only
questions.explanation: TB requires airborne precautions.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When evaluating a teaching session, the best evidence that learning occurred is:
choices: The nurse feels the session went well in this situation
family remained quiet during assessment as the next step
client demonstrates or explains the skill correctly
The handout was distributed at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Return demonstration or accurate teach-back shows learning.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse receives a verbal order during an emergency. Which action is appropriate?
choices: Read back the order per policy and document properly
Ignore the order because it was verbal as the next step
Write the order later from memory at this time for now
Ask another client to witness it for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Read-back helps prevent errors with verbal orders.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which factor most directly increases the risk of falls in hospitalized clients?
choices: Hair length as the next step at this time
Favorite television program at this time
Impaired mobility and altered cognition
Blood type as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: Mobility and cognition strongly affect fall risk.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a postoperative client with fever and purulent drainage. Which step of the nursing process is the nurse using when deciding that the wound may be infected?
choices: Planning next month’s schedule
Assessment and analysis of data
Implementation only as ordered
Evaluation after discharge
questions.explanation: Recognizing concerning findings begins with assessment and analysis.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement about delegation is correct?
choices: Any nursing judgment task may be delegated freely for now as ordered
Accountability transfers completely to the delegatee as ordered during care
nurse remains accountable for the overall outcome of delegated care
Delegation is based only on who volunteers first in this client right away
questions.explanation: Even after delegation, the nurse remains accountable for outcomes and supervision.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When using a restraint as a last resort, the nurse must:
choices: Follow policy, obtain proper authorization, and monitor often
Apply it indefinitely for convenience during care in this client
Avoid reassessment once client is quiet in this client right away
Use it without documentation right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Restraints require strict adherence to policy, monitoring, and documentation.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A student nurse asks what fidelity means in ethics. The best answer is:
choices: Making all decisions alone during care in this client right away at this stage
Doing no harm in this client right away at this stage in this situation
Keeping commitments and being faithful to professional responsibilities
Distributing resources equally at this stage in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Fidelity refers to faithfulness to promises and professional duties.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action is best when a client identifies a different pill than expected?
choices: Give the pill because it is already prepared in this client
Discard client’s concern right away at this stage in this situation
Hold the medication and recheck the order before giving it
Tell client not to question staff in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Medication discrepancies should be checked before administration.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: What is the safest action when a client’s bed alarm sounds and the nurse finds the client trying to stand?
choices: Raise the bed to the highest position right away at this stage
Assist client safely and assess for toileting or other needs
Scold client for moving in this situation during assessment
Turn off the alarm and leave during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Responding promptly and addressing needs can prevent falls.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse notices skin redness over a bony prominence. Which intervention is best?
choices: Massage the area vigorously at this stage
Relieve pressure and reassess the area
Ignore it until the next shift during assessment
Apply adhesive tape tightly as the next step
questions.explanation: Early pressure relief can prevent skin breakdown.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement best describes evidence-based practice?
choices: Using tradition alone in this situation during assessment as the next step
Avoiding research in daily care during assessment as the next step at this time
Integrating best current evidence with clinical expertise and client values
Following whichever method is fastest at this time for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Evidence-based practice combines research evidence, expertise, and client preferences.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which legal concept is involved when a nurse touches a client without consent during a nonemergency procedure?
choices: Slander
Assault only
Libel
Battery
questions.explanation: Unconsented touching may constitute battery.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse is asked to float to another unit and perform an unfamiliar high-risk procedure. What is the best response?
choices: Perform the procedure after watching once as the next step at this time for now
Communicate limitations and request supervision or reassignment to safe tasks
Refuse all care on the unit for now as ordered during care in this client right away
Proceed silently to avoid conflict as ordered during care in this client right away
questions.explanation: The nurse must practice within competence and ask for appropriate support.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action helps maintain a therapeutic nurse-client relationship?
choices: Using empathy while keeping professional boundaries
Sharing intimate personal problems with the client
Accepting expensive gifts from the client as ordered
Meeting the client socially after discharge during care
questions.explanation: Therapeutic relationships require empathy and professional boundaries.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A client with hearing impairment is being taught wound care. Which approach is best?
choices: Face client, speak clearly, and use demonstrations or written support as needed
Shout from the doorway as ordered during care in this client right away at this stage
Avoid visual aids during care in this client right away at this stage in this situation
Talk while turned away in this client right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Facing the client and using clear communication plus demonstration improves understanding.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which task is appropriate to delegate to nursing assistive personnel?
choices: Evaluating response to pain medication as ordered
Obtaining routine vital signs on a stable client
Initial assessment of a new admission in this client
Teaching about insulin injection right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Routine vital signs on a stable client are typically appropriate for delegation.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A client develops redness and itching after starting an antibiotic infusion. What is the priority nursing action?
choices: Document after finishing the dose
Tell the client it is expected and continue
Increase the infusion rate
Stop the infusion and assess the client
questions.explanation: Possible allergic reaction requires stopping the drug and assessing the client promptly.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement about incident reports is correct?
choices: They must be shown to all visitors in this client right away at this stage
They should replace charting right away at this stage in this situation
They are for quality improvement and are not part of client’s chart
They are optional after serious events in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Incident reports support risk management and do not replace clinical documentation.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action is most consistent with justice in nursing ethics?
choices: Giving preferential care only to friends
Withholding information from difficult clients
Ignoring disparities in access in this situation
Providing fair and equitable care based on need
questions.explanation: Justice involves fairness and equitable treatment.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: When using PPE to remove soiled linen, which action helps prevent contamination?
choices: Sort linen in the hallway at this stage in this situation
Shake linen vigorously to remove dust in this situation
Place linen on the floor first during assessment
Hold linen away from the body and avoid shaking it
questions.explanation: Handling linen away from the body without shaking reduces spread of microorganisms.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: The nurse is evaluating whether a client can safely learn self-injection. Which factor is most important?
choices: The nurse’s shift preference in this situation
The room number during assessment as the next step
The color of the syringe cap as the next step
client’s readiness, cognition, and motor ability
questions.explanation: Readiness and ability determine whether self-administration teaching will be successful.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement best describes advocacy?
choices: Protecting client’s rights and helping client express informed choices
Agreeing with every request even when unsafe as the next step at this time
Keeping silent about unsafe orders at this time for now as ordered during care
Making decisions without consulting client for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Advocacy means supporting clients’ rights and informed decisions.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse prepares a sterile field and then turns away to answer the phone. The field should be considered:
choices: Contaminated and replaced
Usable if covered later
Still sterile if untouched
Sterile for 30 more minutes
questions.explanation: A sterile field left unattended is considered contaminated.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action is appropriate when documenting a late entry?
choices: Label it as a late entry and record the actual time and date appropriately
Insert it in the record without notation for now as ordered during care in this client
Change the earlier chart time to match as ordered during care in this client
Erase the previous note during care in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Late entries should be clearly labeled and dated/timed properly.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action helps reduce needlestick injuries?
choices: Carry used sharps in a pocket for now as ordered during care in this client right away
Place sharps on bedside tables as ordered during care in this client right away at this stage
Recap used needles with two hands during care in this client right away at this stage
Activate safety devices and dispose of sharps promptly in puncture-resistant containers
questions.explanation: Sharps safety devices and prompt disposal reduce injury risk.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse is assigned to four clients. Which task should be done first?
choices: Deliver a routine water pitcher as ordered during care
Assess client reporting sudden shortness of breath
Refold clean linens in this client right away at this stage
Restock nonurgent supplies right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Sudden shortness of breath suggests an urgent change in status.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which question is best when assessing a client’s learning needs?
choices: Would you rather skip teaching today and forever? during care
Why do clients never listen? in this client right away at this stage
Do you promise to memorize all instructions? right away
What concerns you most about caring for yourself at home?
questions.explanation: Assessment of learning needs starts with the client’s concerns and priorities.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action by the nurse best supports continuity of care at discharge?
choices: Assume discharge teaching is unnecessary if client looks confident in this client
Rely only on family memory right away at this stage in this situation during assessment
Send client home without written information at this stage in this situation
give clear instructions, verify understanding, and arrange follow-up as needed
questions.explanation: Clear discharge teaching and follow-up planning support continuity and safety.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which action is correct when documenting an electronic health record password?
choices: Share it with coworkers on busy days
Keep it confidential and never share it
Post it at the nurses’ station for convenience
Use the same simple password for every system and tell the unit
questions.explanation: Passwords protect security and must remain confidential.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse caring for multiple clients should use SBAR mainly to:
choices: Communicate essential information clearly and efficiently
Document only normal findings in this situation during assessment
Replace all charting permanently during assessment as the next step
Avoid talking with physicians as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: SBAR is a structured format for clear clinical communication.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which statement about the nursing process is correct?
choices: It ends after assessment in this situation during assessment
It prevents the need for evaluation during assessment
It is used only by administrators as the next step
It is a systematic framework for individualized care
questions.explanation: The nursing process guides assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A nurse receives an order that seems unsafe. What is the best action?
choices: Question the order and seek clarification before carrying it out
Carry it out quickly to avoid delay as the next step at this time
Ignore the concern and hope for the best at this time for now as ordered
Ask an unlicensed person to decide for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: The nurse must clarify unsafe orders to protect the client.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: Which client teaching point is most important after administering sedating medication?
choices: Call for assistance before getting out of bed
Walk alone in the hallway immediately at this time
Remove nonskid footwear for now as ordered
Drink alcohol to sleep better as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Sedation increases fall risk, so assistance is important.
questions.category: Fundamentals of Nursing including Professional Adjustments

questions.question: A primipara is 1 hour postpartum. The uterus is boggy and deviated to the right. What should the nurse do first?
choices: Start oxygen at 10 L/min via mask at this time
Administer a tocolytic medication for now as ordered
Prepare the client for immediate surgery as ordered
Massage the fundus and assess bladder distention
questions.explanation: A boggy uterus suggests uterine atony; the nurse first massages the fundus and checks whether a full bladder is displacing the uterus.

questions.question: During the fourth stage of labor, which finding requires immediate nursing action?
choices: Mild afterpains during breastfeeding
Pulse rate of 58 beats/min as ordered
Temperature of 37.4°C (99.3°F)
Saturated perineal pad in 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Heavy lochia with rapid pad saturation suggests postpartum hemorrhage and requires immediate intervention.

questions.question: A woman at 32 weeks’ gestation reports painless vaginal bleeding. Best action?
choices: Prepare for external cephalic version as ordered
Perform a sterile vaginal examination during care
Assess fetal heart rate and place client on bed rest
Encourage client to ambulate right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Painless bleeding in late pregnancy suggests placenta previa; fetal status should be checked and vaginal examination avoided.

questions.question: A laboring client suddenly complains of severe abdominal pain and has fetal bradycardia. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
choices: False labor
Mild placental calcification
Round ligament pain
Uterine rupture
questions.explanation: Sudden pain with fetal distress in labor is a classic emergency sign of uterine rupture.

questions.question: Which finding is expected in a newborn during the first 24 hours after birth?
choices: Persistent central cyanosis
No urinary output right away
Absent Moro reflex at this stage
Acrocyanosis of hands and feet
questions.explanation: Acrocyanosis is a common transitional finding in the first day of life; central cyanosis is abnormal.

questions.question: A newborn has a respiratory rate of 72/min with grunting and nasal flaring. Priority action?
choices: Administer oral glucose water right away at this stage
Report the findings and give prompt respiratory support
Place newborn prone and recheck in 8 hours in this situation
Delay assessment until after feeding during assessment
questions.explanation: Tachypnea with grunting and flaring suggests respiratory distress and requires prompt evaluation and support.

questions.question: Which vaccine is routinely given at birth in the Philippines according to standard newborn care policies?
choices: Varicella and influenza vaccine
DPT and MMR vaccine
BCG and hepatitis B vaccine
Measles and oral polio vaccine
questions.explanation: Routine newborn immunization includes BCG and hepatitis B at birth in standard programs.

questions.question: A postpartum mother with rubella non-immunity asks when she can receive immunization. Best response?
choices: You can receive the rubella vaccine before discharge if you are not pregnant again
You should receive it only after your next pregnancy during assessment as the next step
You should wait until baby is 1 year old as the next step at this time for now
You cannot receive it while breastfeeding at this time for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Rubella vaccine is given postpartum to non-immune mothers and is not contraindicated by breastfeeding.

questions.question: A client in active labor is receiving oxytocin infusion. Which finding requires the nurse to stop the infusion immediately?
choices: Fetal heart rate 140/min with moderate variability
Maternal request for ice chips as the next step at this time
Cervix dilated to 5 cm at this time for now as ordered
Contractions lasting 95 seconds occurring every 2 minutes
questions.explanation: Tachysystole from oxytocin can reduce uteroplacental perfusion; prolonged frequent contractions require stopping the infusion.

questions.question: Which statement by a breastfeeding mother indicates correct understanding of effective latch-on?
choices: Breastfeeding should be painless from the first second
I should hear loud clicking sounds with each suck
My baby should take in the nipple and much of areola
My baby should suck only the nipple tip as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Effective latch includes the nipple and much of the areola; nipple-tip sucking leads to pain and poor milk transfer.

questions.question: A child with acute glomerulonephritis is admitted with periorbital edema and hypertension. Which intervention is most important?
choices: Maintain strict bed rest for two weeks in all cases
Encourage unrestricted oral fluids
Monitor blood pressure and fluid status closely
Provide a high-sodium snack
questions.explanation: Fluid overload and hypertension are key concerns in acute glomerulonephritis and require close monitoring.

questions.question: The nurse is teaching a mother about oral rehydration for a child with mild diarrhea. Which instruction is correct?
choices: Offer only carbonated soft drinks for now as ordered
Give small, regular sips of oral rehydration solution
Stop all feeding for 24 hours during care in this client
Use plain water alone for replacement in this client
questions.explanation: ORS should be given in small, frequent amounts to replace losses while feeding is generally continued.

questions.question: Which sign is the best indicator of severe dehydration in an infant?
choices: Tears when crying
Moist oral mucosa
Sunken fontanel and lethargy
Capillary refill under 2 seconds
questions.explanation: Sunken fontanel with lethargy points to significant dehydration in infants.

questions.question: A child with measles is hospitalized. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
choices: Give live vaccine during the acute illness during care in this client
give aspirin for fever control in this client right away
Institute airborne precautions and monitor for complications
Encourage bright light exposure at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Measles requires airborne isolation and supportive monitoring; aspirin is avoided in children with viral illnesses.

questions.question: A pregnant client asks why iron supplementation is prescribed. Which explanation is best?
choices: It helps prevent maternal anemia and supports increased red blood cell production
It will stop morning sickness at once right away at this stage in this situation
It guarantees a larger birth weight at this stage in this situation during assessment
It prevents all types of congenital anomalies in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Pregnancy increases iron requirements because of expanding maternal blood volume and fetal needs.

questions.question: Which finding in a client with severe preeclampsia should the nurse report immediately?
choices: Urinary frequency in the third trimester
Epigastric pain and visual disturbances
Fetal movement felt after meals
Dependent ankle edema at the end of the day
questions.explanation: Epigastric pain and visual changes suggest worsening severe preeclampsia and possible eclamptic complications.

questions.question: The nurse is caring for a client after amniotomy. Which assessment is the priority immediately after the procedure?
choices: Cervical dilation
Maternal temperature
Fetal heart rate
Pain score
questions.explanation: After membrane rupture, the immediate priority is fetal heart rate assessment because cord prolapse can occur.

questions.question: Which sign most strongly suggests placental separation during the third stage of labor?
choices: A gush of blood with cord lengthening
Regular contractions every 10 minutes
Maternal complaint of thirst as the next step
Fetal head crowning at this time for now
questions.explanation: Placental separation is indicated by a gush of blood, fundal rise, and lengthening of the cord.

questions.question: A neonate born to a diabetic mother is jittery and weak. What should the nurse suspect first?
choices: Necrotizing enterocolitis
Hypoglycemia
Polycythemia crisis
Hypercalcemia
questions.explanation: Jitteriness and weakness soon after birth in an infant of a diabetic mother commonly indicate hypoglycemia.

questions.question: Which statement by the mother of a child with febrile seizure needs further teaching?
choices: I should note how long the seizure lasts
I should restrain my child tightly during the seizure
I should keep objects away from my child
I should place my child on the side during the seizure
questions.explanation: The child should not be restrained tightly during a seizure because it can cause injury.

questions.question: When teaching a postpartum client about lochia, which statement is correct?
choices: Large clots are expected every day at this time for now as ordered
Lochia remains bright red for six weeks for now as ordered
Lochia should gradually change from rubra to serosa to alba
A foul odor is a normal sign of healing during care in this client
questions.explanation: Normal lochia progresses from rubra to serosa to alba; persistent bright red bleeding or foul odor is abnormal.

questions.question: The nurse is assessing fetal well-being during labor. Which finding is most reassuring?
choices: Late decelerations after each contraction for now as ordered
Persistent fetal bradycardia at 100/min as ordered during care
Baseline fetal heart rate of 140/min with moderate variability
Absent variability for 30 minutes in this client right away
questions.explanation: A normal baseline with moderate variability is a reassuring sign of adequate fetal oxygenation.

questions.question: A postpartum client reports calf pain and warmth. Which action should the nurse take first?
choices: Massage the affected calf as ordered during care in this client right away
Assess for signs of deep vein thrombosis and keep client on bed rest
Place client in Trendelenburg position in this client right away
Apply a heating pad and encourage walking right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Calf pain and warmth raise concern for DVT; massage and ambulation could dislodge a clot.

questions.question: Which instruction is best when teaching a mother how to prevent neonatal hypothermia at home?
choices: Keep baby dry, clothed, and in skin-to-skin contact when appropriate
Bathe baby in cool water daily in this client right away at this stage
Place the crib near an open window for ventilation right away at this stage
Leave the head uncovered indoors at this stage in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Drying, covering, and skin-to-skin contact help maintain newborn temperature.

questions.question: A client at 38 weeks has blood pressure 160/110 mmHg and hyperreflexia. What medication is commonly prepared to prevent seizures?
choices: Terbutaline
Magnesium sulfate
Oxytocin at this stage
Methylergometrine
questions.explanation: Magnesium sulfate is used for seizure prophylaxis in severe preeclampsia.

questions.question: Which finding is the earliest sign of increased intracranial pressure in an infant with meningitis?
choices: Decerebrate posturing
Fixed dilated pupils
Bulging fontanel
Absent gag reflex
questions.explanation: A bulging fontanel is an early sign of increased intracranial pressure in infants.

questions.question: A child with nephrotic syndrome is admitted with generalized edema. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?
choices: Encourage a high-sodium diet at this stage
Avoid all immunizations permanently
Restrict protein completely during assessment
