questions.question: Which household waste practice should the nurse most strongly discourage?
choices: Open burning of trash near homes
Participating in scheduled collection
Segregating biodegradables and recyclables
Using covered bins
questions.explanation: Open burning increases pollution and health risks.

questions.question: Which client in an evacuation center should the nurse assess first?
choices: An adult asking about meal schedule at this stage
A man requesting extra blankets in this situation
A child with fast breathing and chest indrawing
A teenager with mild mosquito bites as the next step
questions.explanation: Fast breathing with chest indrawing suggests respiratory distress and needs urgent assessment.

questions.question: The nurse is reviewing causes of maternal mortality in a municipality. Which delay model factor should receive priority if mothers arrive late to facilities?
choices: Delay in deciding to seek care or reaching care
Delay in buying infant clothes during assessment
Delay in planting crops as the next step at this time
Delay in school enrollment at this time for now
questions.explanation: The three delays model highlights delay in deciding, reaching, or receiving care.

questions.question: Which action best supports integrated management of childhood illness in the community?
choices: Assess danger signs, classify illness, counsel caregivers, and arrange follow-up
Focus only on laboratory values as the next step at this time for now as ordered
Ignore nutrition during illness at this time for now as ordered during care in this client
Treat every fever as the same disease for now as ordered during care in this client
questions.explanation: IMCI emphasizes assessment, classification, counseling, treatment, and follow-up.

questions.question: A mother asks when to seek medical care for a child with diarrhea. Which answer is best?
choices: Seek care only if diarrhea lasts one month as the next step at this time for now
Do not seek care if ORS is available at this time for now as ordered during care
Wait until blood appears and fever becomes very high for now as ordered during care
Seek care for persistent vomiting, lethargy, sunken eyes, or inability to drink
questions.explanation: Danger signs such as lethargy, inability to drink, or persistent vomiting require medical evaluation.

questions.question: A client with suspected myocardial infarction reports chest pain unrelieved by rest. Which action is the priority?
choices: Encourage client to walk to the bathroom at this time for now as ordered during care in this client
Obtain vital signs, give oxygen as indicated, and notify the physician or rapid response team
Place client flat and give a large meal as ordered during care in this client right away
Delay assessment until family arrives during care in this client right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Potential acute coronary syndrome requires immediate assessment and rapid intervention.

questions.question: Which assessment finding is most concerning in a client receiving a blood transfusion?
choices: Mild thirst before the transfusion
A pulse that decreases after pain relief
Sleepiness late at night
Fever, chills, and low back pain
questions.explanation: Fever, chills, and back pain may indicate a transfusion reaction and require stopping the transfusion.

questions.question: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is most appropriately positioned to ease breathing in:
choices: Prone position with legs elevated
Flat supine position
Trendelenburg position
High Fowler’s or tripod position
questions.explanation: Upright positioning improves diaphragmatic movement and ventilation in COPD.

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a client with increased intracranial pressure. Which action should be avoided?
choices: Minimizing noxious stimulation
regular hip flexion and neck flexion
Keeping the head midline right away
Elevating the head of bed as ordered
questions.explanation: Hip and neck flexion can increase intrathoracic pressure and worsen intracranial pressure.

questions.question: Which finding most strongly suggests hypovolemic shock?
choices: Slow capillary refill with severe hypertension
Cool clammy skin, tachycardia, and hypotension
Bradycardia with hypertension at this stage
Bounding pulse with warm dry skin in this situation
questions.explanation: Hypovolemic shock commonly presents with tachycardia, hypotension, and cool clammy skin.

questions.question: A client with diabetes asks why foot inspection is important. Which response is best?
choices: It replaces the need for proper footwear right away at this stage in this situation
Neuropathy can reduce sensation, so injuries may go unnoticed and become infected
It prevents all blood sugar changes in this situation during assessment as the next step
It is only necessary for athletes during assessment as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: Neuropathy and poor circulation make foot injury and infection more likely in diabetes.

questions.question: Which laboratory value requires the nurse to question administration of potassium chloride?
choices: Platelet count 250,000/mm3
Hemoglobin 13 g/dL
Serum sodium 138 mEq/L
Serum potassium 5.8 mEq/L
questions.explanation: Potassium should be withheld in hyperkalemia because it can worsen cardiac risk.

questions.question: A postoperative client suddenly develops shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain. What complication should the nurse suspect?
choices: Wound evisceration
Constipation
Pulmonary embolism
Mild atelectasis only
questions.explanation: Acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain after surgery suggest pulmonary embolism.

questions.question: Which intervention is most important for preventing pressure injuries in an immobile client?
choices: Regular repositioning and skin assessment
Using donut rings continuously
Limiting protein intake
Massaging reddened bony prominences vigorously
questions.explanation: Regular repositioning and inspection help prevent pressure injury development.

questions.question: A client with congestive heart failure has crackles and dyspnea. Which action by the nurse is priority?
choices: Position upright and assess oxygenation
Delay assessment until the next shift
Keep the client flat in bed for now as ordered
Encourage rapid fluid intake as ordered
questions.explanation: Upright positioning and oxygenation assessment are immediate priorities in fluid overload.

questions.question: The nurse is monitoring a client receiving heparin. Which laboratory test is most useful?
choices: Activated partial thromboplastin time
Clot retraction time for now as ordered
Bleeding time as ordered during care
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
questions.explanation: aPTT is used to monitor unfractionated heparin therapy.

questions.question: Which sign is most characteristic of a client with hypoglycemia?
choices: Dry skin and deep respirations
Diaphoresis, tremors, and confusion
Bradycardia with flushed skin
Polyuria with fruity breath only
questions.explanation: Adrenergic and neuroglycopenic symptoms such as sweating, tremor, and confusion suggest hypoglycemia.

questions.question: A client with acute appendicitis should be placed on which diet while awaiting surgery?
choices: High-fiber diet
Clear liquids every hour
NPO status
Regular diet as tolerated
questions.explanation: The client is kept NPO in preparation for possible surgery and to reduce aspiration risk.

questions.question: Which nursing measure helps prevent deep vein thrombosis in a postoperative client?
choices: Restricting fluids to thicken the blood
Placing pillows behind the knees continuously
Massaging calf muscles every shift
Early ambulation and leg exercises
questions.explanation: Early ambulation and leg exercises promote venous return and reduce DVT risk.

questions.question: Which sign suggests fluid overload in a client receiving IV therapy?
choices: Poor skin turgor and tachycardia
Sunken eyes and concentrated urine
Dry mucous membranes and hypotension
Neck vein distention and crackles
questions.explanation: JVD and crackles point to excess intravascular volume and pulmonary congestion.

questions.question: A client with renal failure has peaked T waves on ECG. Which electrolyte imbalance should the nurse suspect?
choices: Hypokalemia
Hyperkalemia
Hypercalcemia
Hyponatremia
questions.explanation: Peaked T waves are a classic sign of hyperkalemia.

questions.question: Which action is most appropriate when caring for a client with a chest tube drainage system?
choices: Clamp the tube routinely during transport
Keep the drainage system below chest level
Raise the drainage system onto the bed
Milk the tubing vigorously every hour
questions.explanation: The drainage unit should stay below chest level to promote drainage and prevent backflow.

questions.question: A burn client’s first priority during the emergent phase is:
choices: Airway and breathing assessment
Scar management teaching
Range-of-motion exercises
High-protein menu selection
questions.explanation: During the emergent phase of burns, airway and breathing are immediate priorities.

questions.question: Which finding in a client with a fractured femur suggests fat embolism syndrome?
choices: Constipation from immobility during assessment
Localized bruising at the fracture site
Sudden hypoxia, confusion, and petechiae
Mild pain relieved by rest for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Fat embolism often presents with respiratory distress, neurologic changes, and petechiae.

questions.question: A client with liver cirrhosis is at risk for bleeding mainly because of:
choices: Increased calcium absorption
Enhanced platelet synthesis
Reduced clotting factor production
Excess hemoglobin formation
questions.explanation: The diseased liver produces fewer clotting factors, increasing bleeding risk.

questions.question: Which assessment is the priority before giving digoxin to an adult client?
choices: Apical pulse for one full minute
Pedal pulse for 10 seconds
Respiratory rate only as ordered
Temperature only during care in this client
questions.explanation: The apical pulse should be assessed before digoxin because bradycardia may require holding the drug.

questions.question: A client with asthma is wheezing and using accessory muscles. Which medication should the nurse expect for rapid relief?
choices: A stool softener for now as ordered
An oral iron supplement
A topical antifungal during care
A short-acting bronchodilator
questions.explanation: Short-acting bronchodilators provide quick relief of acute bronchospasm.

questions.question: Which finding indicates that peritoneal dialysis is not draining properly?
choices: Improved breathing after fluid removal as ordered during care
Cloudy or inadequate outflow with abdominal discomfort
Light yellow outflow with expected volume in this client
A slightly warm dialysate bag before infusion right away
questions.explanation: Poor or cloudy drainage with discomfort suggests a problem such as obstruction or peritonitis.

questions.question: Which instruction is best for a client taking warfarin at home?
choices: Double the dose after a missed tablet without advice during care
Stop the drug whenever bruising appears mild in this client
Avoid all green vegetables permanently right away at this stage
Report unusual bleeding and keep vitamin K intake consistent
questions.explanation: Warfarin requires bleeding precautions and a consistent, not absent, vitamin K intake.

questions.question: A client with stroke has dysphagia. Which nursing action best reduces aspiration risk?
choices: Offer thin liquids quickly through a straw in this client right away
Keep client upright during meals and use swallowing precautions
Feed large bites to shorten mealtime at this stage in this situation
Place client flat after feeding in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Upright positioning and prescribed swallowing precautions reduce aspiration.

questions.question: Which symptom is most typical of a client with left-sided heart failure?
choices: Cool feet without lung findings
Pulmonary congestion and dyspnea
Massive ascites without dyspnea
Marked jugular venous distention only
questions.explanation: Left-sided heart failure typically causes pulmonary congestion and shortness of breath.

questions.question: A client with acute pancreatitis should initially receive which diet?
choices: Unrestricted alcohol at this stage
High-fat regular diet in this situation
Large frequent meals during assessment
NPO with IV fluids as prescribed
questions.explanation: Resting the pancreas with NPO status is common in acute pancreatitis management.

questions.question: Which action is essential when administering enteral feeding through a tube?
choices: Warm formula in a microwave until very hot
Verify placement and assess residuals per policy
Lay the client flat during feeding as the next step
Add medication directly without flushing at this time
questions.explanation: Placement verification and proper feeding technique reduce aspiration risk.

questions.question: A client with nephrolithiasis reports severe flank pain. Which intervention is appropriate?
choices: Delay pain assessment until imaging returns during assessment
Apply pressure directly over the kidney as the next step at this time
Encourage fluids if not contraindicated and strain the urine
Restrict all oral intake indefinitely for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Fluid intake and urine straining help stone passage and identification when not contraindicated.

questions.question: Which sign suggests compartment syndrome after a cast is applied?
choices: Warm fingers with brisk capillary refill
Ability to move digits easily at this time for now
Pain unrelieved by medication with paresthesia
Mild itching under the cast as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Severe pain with paresthesia may signal compartment syndrome, a surgical emergency.

questions.question: A client with thyroid storm requires priority monitoring for:
choices: Mild weight gain at this time for now as ordered
Hyperthermia and cardiovascular instability
Cold intolerance only as ordered during care
Constipation without tachycardia during care
questions.explanation: Thyroid storm can cause severe fever, tachycardia, and life-threatening instability.

questions.question: Which intervention is appropriate for a client with seizure disorder during an active seizure?
choices: Insert a tongue blade between the teeth for now as ordered
Force oral medication at once as ordered during care
Restrain all limbs tightly during care in this client right away
Protect client from injury and maintain airway as possible
questions.explanation: The focus during a seizure is safety and airway protection; objects should not be placed in the mouth.

questions.question: A client with gastric ulcer disease asks why NSAIDs should be avoided. Which explanation is best?
choices: They increase appetite without risk as ordered during care in this client
They improve platelet clotting during care in this client right away
They permanently cure ulcer disease in this client right away
They can irritate the gastric mucosa and worsen bleeding risk
questions.explanation: NSAIDs can damage gastric mucosa and worsen ulcer bleeding.

questions.question: Which finding in a client with meningitis should be reported immediately?
choices: Anorexia after breakfast during care
Soreness at IV site in this client
Decreasing level of consciousness
Mild headache relieved by rest
questions.explanation: Worsening neurologic status requires urgent attention in meningitis.

questions.question: A client with anemia reports fatigue. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate initially?
choices: Plan care to allow rest between activities
Keep lights on all night
Restrict iron-rich foods
Encourage strenuous exercise to build stamina quickly
questions.explanation: Fatigue from anemia often improves when activity is balanced with rest.

questions.question: A client with urinary retention has a prescription for intermittent catheterization. What is the main purpose?
choices: To empty the bladder and reduce overdistention
To increase bowel motility at this stage in this situation
To improve hearing acuity in this situation
To test visual fields during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Intermittent catheterization relieves retention and protects bladder function.

questions.question: A nurse is teaching a client with GERD. Which instruction is best?
choices: Increase caffeine intake at this stage in this situation during assessment
Take meals just before bedtime in this situation during assessment
Avoid lying down right after meals and elevate the head of bed
Wear tight abdominal garments as the next step at this time
questions.explanation: Lifestyle measures for GERD include avoiding recumbency after meals and head-of-bed elevation.

questions.question: A client with chronic kidney disease has pruritus. Which intervention may help?
choices: give skin care, keep nails short, and use mild emollients
Apply heavily scented alcohol-based lotion frequently
Use very hot baths daily as the next step at this time for now
Discourage fluid balance monitoring at this time for now
questions.explanation: Gentle skin care and emollients help reduce pruritus in kidney disease.

questions.question: Which finding suggests that a diabetic client understands sick-day management?
choices: I will drink no fluids to avoid vomiting during assessment as the next step
I will continue prescribed insulin and monitor glucose more often
I will stop insulin whenever I cannot eat full meals at this time
I will ignore urine ketones during illness for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Illness often raises glucose, so insulin and monitoring usually continue with hydration.

questions.question: Which intervention is most appropriate for a client with suspected spinal cord injury?
choices: Sit the client upright immediately
Immobilize the spine and avoid unnecessary movement
Place a pillow under the shoulders and twist the trunk
Encourage neck exercises
questions.explanation: Spinal precautions prevent further neurologic injury.

questions.question: Which manifestation is expected in a client with hyperthyroidism?
choices: Dry thick skin without palpitations
Heat intolerance and tachycardia
Cold intolerance and bradycardia
Weight gain with slowed speech only
questions.explanation: Hyperthyroidism commonly causes heat intolerance, tachycardia, and weight loss.

questions.question: A client with bowel obstruction has a nasogastric tube. The main purpose of the tube is to:
choices: Decompress the stomach and reduce vomiting
Measure blood pressure continuously
Provide long-term bladder drainage during care
Administer intramuscular medication
questions.explanation: NG decompression reduces gastric distention and vomiting in bowel obstruction.

questions.question: Which action is correct when collecting a sterile urine specimen from an indwelling catheter?
choices: Disconnect the catheter from the bag and pour urine into a cup as ordered during care
Open the system below the bladder during care in this client right away at this stage
Clamp briefly if ordered, cleanse the port, and aspirate from the sampling port
Obtain urine from the drainage bag after several hours right away at this stage
questions.explanation: A specimen should be taken aseptically from the sampling port, not the drainage bag.

questions.question: A client with severe hypertension develops headache and blurred vision. Which complication is the nurse most concerned about?
choices: Hypertensive crisis with target-organ damage
Expected medication effect in this client right away
Simple tension headache right away at this stage
Mild dehydration at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Neurologic symptoms with severe hypertension may indicate hypertensive crisis.

questions.question: A nurse is teaching about inhaler use. Which step is important with inhaled corticosteroids?
choices: Use it to stop acute anaphylaxis
Take the medication only when chest pain occurs
Store the canister in hot water
Rinse the mouth after use
questions.explanation: Rinsing after inhaled steroids helps reduce oral candidiasis.

questions.question: Which finding in a post-thyroidectomy client requires immediate intervention?
choices: Mild incisional soreness
Stridor and respiratory difficulty
Small amount of serosanguinous drainage
Hoarse voice that improves with rest
questions.explanation: Stridor may indicate airway obstruction and is a postoperative emergency.

questions.question: A client with peripheral arterial disease should be taught to:
choices: Apply direct heat to numb feet
Elevate legs above the heart for long periods
Avoid crossing legs and stop smoking
Walk barefoot indoors for comfort
questions.explanation: Smoking cessation and avoiding impaired circulation behaviors are important in arterial disease.

questions.question: Which action best prevents infection in a surgical wound?
choices: Perform hand hygiene and maintain aseptic dressing changes
Clean from the dirtiest area to the cleanest during assessment
Reuse soiled dressing supplies as the next step at this time
Remove drains with bare hands at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene and aseptic technique are fundamental for preventing wound infection.

questions.question: A client with Cushing syndrome is likely to exhibit:
choices: Cold intolerance and constipation during assessment
Tetany and positive Chvostek sign as the next step
Severe weight loss with hypotension only
Hyperglycemia and increased infection risk
questions.explanation: Excess cortisol can raise glucose and suppress immune response.

questions.question: Which assessment finding suggests improvement in a client treated for pneumonia?
choices: Increasing crackles with cyanosis
Rising respiratory rate and confusion
New pleuritic pain and hemoptysis
Decreased fever and easier breathing
questions.explanation: Clinical improvement in pneumonia includes reduced fever and better ventilation.

questions.question: A client with ileostomy requires teaching. Which statement is correct?
choices: Stool from an ileostomy is usually liquid to semi-liquid
The pouch is unnecessary if output is small for now as ordered
The stoma should be scrubbed with alcohol daily as ordered
The stoma should appear black during care in this client
questions.explanation: Ileostomy output is generally liquid or semi-liquid.

questions.question: A client with Addison disease is most at risk for:
choices: Severe hypernatremia
Marked hypertension from cortisol excess
Hypotension and hyperkalemia
Persistent tachycardia with hyperglycemia only
questions.explanation: Adrenal insufficiency can cause low blood pressure and high potassium.

questions.question: Which action is best when caring for a client with neutropenia?
choices: Limit oral hygiene as ordered during care in this client right away
Take rectal temperatures routinely during care in this client right away
Monitor for infection and use protective precautions as indicated
Serve raw fruits without washing right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Neutropenic clients need infection prevention and careful monitoring.

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a client receiving morphine IV. Which assessment is the priority before administration?
choices: Dominant hand during care in this client
Respiratory rate and level of sedation
Bowel pattern from last month right away
Hair color at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Opioids can depress respiration, so respiratory assessment is critical.

questions.question: A client with glaucoma should be taught that the goal of treatment is to:
choices: Reduce ear pressure in this client right away
Whiten the sclera right away at this stage in this situation
Restore lost vision immediately in all cases
Lower intraocular pressure and preserve vision
questions.explanation: Glaucoma treatment aims to lower intraocular pressure and slow vision loss.

questions.question: Which measure is most important to prevent falls in an older adult with confusion?
choices: Darken the room completely right away at this stage in this situation
Keep often used items within reach and give close supervision
Restrain client continuously in this situation during assessment
Raise all four side rails and leave unattended during assessment
questions.explanation: Environmental safety and supervision are effective fall-prevention measures.

questions.question: A client with a positive Trousseau sign most likely has:
choices: Hypernatremia
Hypocalcemia
Hypermagnesemia
Polycythemia
questions.explanation: Trousseau sign indicates neuromuscular irritability associated with low calcium.

questions.question: A client with acute kidney injury has very low urine output. Which finding requires urgent reporting?
choices: Slight ankle itching in this situation
Mild thirst during assessment as the next step
Shortness of breath with crackles
Preference for warm blankets
questions.explanation: Oliguria with crackles suggests fluid overload affecting the lungs.

questions.question: A client with ulcerative colitis is in an acute flare. Which diet is commonly appropriate?
choices: Spicy fried foods
High-fiber bran with seeds
Low-residue diet as prescribed
Large servings of raw vegetables
questions.explanation: A low-residue diet may reduce bowel irritation during a flare.

questions.question: A client with severe vomiting has metabolic alkalosis. Which assessment finding is expected?
choices: A fruity odor to the breath from ketones
Slow shallow breathing as compensation
Severe diarrhea as the main cause
Kussmaul respirations
questions.explanation: Metabolic alkalosis may lead to compensatory hypoventilation to retain carbon dioxide.

questions.question: A client says, “I hear voices telling me to hurt myself.” What is the nurse’s priority response?
choices: Encourage client to argue with the voices alone at this time
Tell client the voices are not real and walk away for now
Assess the content of hallucinations and ensure prompt safety
Ignore the statement unless family confirms it during care
questions.explanation: Command hallucinations require immediate safety assessment and intervention.

questions.question: Which communication technique is therapeutic when a depressed client says, “Nothing matters anymore”?
choices: Tell me more about what you are feeling right now
Let us not talk about sad things as ordered during care
You should not feel that way during care in this client
Others have it worse than you in this client right away
questions.explanation: Open-ended exploration encourages expression and conveys acceptance.

questions.question: A client with mania is pacing constantly and intruding on others. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?
choices: Set clear limits and give a low-stimulation environment
Encourage group games with many rules during care in this client
Offer caffeinated drinks to increase focus in this client
Reason at length during peak agitation right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Clients with mania need limit setting and reduced stimulation.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of a no-suicide or safety plan?
choices: It replaces ongoing assessment during care in this client right away
It is one part of broader suicide risk management and follow-up
It guarantees that client will not self-harm right away at this stage
It is unnecessary once mood improves for one hour at this stage
questions.explanation: A safety plan supports but does not replace full suicide risk assessment and management.

questions.question: A client with paranoid delusions states, “The staff are poisoning my food.” What is the best nursing response?
choices: I understand that you feel unsafe; let us look at ways to help you eat comfortably
If you do not eat, you will be punished right away at this stage in this situation
You are correct, the kitchen is dangerous at this stage in this situation during assessment
That is ridiculous and impossible in this situation during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: The nurse acknowledges feelings without validating the delusion and works toward practical support.

questions.question: Which behavior is most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder?
choices: Sudden flashbacks after trauma only right away at this stage in this situation
Hearing voices commenting on actions at this stage in this situation
Repetitive handwashing to reduce anxiety despite skin irritation
Alternating periods of mania and depression during assessment as the next step
questions.explanation: Compulsions are repetitive behaviors performed to reduce anxiety.

questions.question: A client taking lithium should be taught to report which sign immediately?
choices: Occasional hunger before lunch at this stage
A desire to drink water on a hot day
Mild thirst after exercise during assessment
Severe diarrhea, vomiting, and tremors
questions.explanation: GI upset and tremors may signal lithium toxicity and need prompt evaluation.

questions.question: The nurse is caring for a client in alcohol withdrawal. Which finding requires immediate intervention?
choices: Mild fatigue in this situation during assessment
Increased appetite during assessment as the next step
A request for quiet music as the next step
Seizures or severe autonomic instability
questions.explanation: Alcohol withdrawal can progress to life-threatening seizures or delirium tremens.

questions.question: Which intervention is best for a client experiencing a panic attack?
choices: Discuss childhood conflicts in detail at once during assessment
Stay with client, speak calmly, and reduce environmental stimuli
Leave client alone to gain control at this time for now as ordered
Argue that there is nothing to fear for now as ordered during care
questions.explanation: During panic, the nurse should remain calm, stay with the client, and reduce stimuli.

questions.question: Which statement by the nurse best promotes trust with a client diagnosed with borderline personality disorder?
choices: I will bend the rules whenever you are upset as the next step at this time
I will be consistent with the plan and let you know what to expect
You can decide the rules for the whole unit for now as ordered during care
I will keep secrets from the team if you ask as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Consistency and clear boundaries help build trust and reduce splitting.

questions.question: A client with schizophrenia is withdrawn and neglecting hygiene. Which symptom type is this?
choices: Command hallucination
Flight of ideas
Obsessive compulsion
Negative symptom
questions.explanation: Avolition and poor self-care are negative symptoms of schizophrenia.

questions.question: Which action is most important when administering haloperidol IM to an agitated client?
choices: Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms and ensure safety
Encourage sunbathing immediately after the injection
Expect the drug to improve nutrition instantly
Offer grapefruit juice with each dose in this client
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics like haloperidol can cause extrapyramidal side effects that require monitoring.

questions.question: A client with post-traumatic stress disorder reports nightmares and hypervigilance. Which nursing approach is most helpful initially?
choices: Force detailed retelling of trauma right away as ordered during care
give a calm environment and encourage grounding and coping skills
Use confrontation to challenge fear responses in this client right away
Discourage all discussion of symptoms right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Early supportive care includes safety, grounding, and coping strategies.

questions.question: When working with a client who has anorexia nervosa, which nursing priority is most important?
choices: Monitor nutritional status and physiologic stability
Praise extreme weight loss as self-control in this client
Ignore food rituals to avoid conflict right away at this stage
Allow unlimited exercise after meals at this stage
questions.explanation: Physiologic stability and nutrition are priority concerns in anorexia nervosa.

questions.question: A client says, “I just want to go to sleep and never wake up.” What is the nurse’s best first action?
choices: Leave client alone to rest in this client right away
Change the subject to improve mood right away at this stage
Assess directly for suicidal intent, plan, and means
Promise secrecy in this situation during assessment
questions.explanation: Direct suicide assessment is indicated when a client expresses hopeless or death-related thoughts.

questions.question: Which response is therapeutic when a grieving client cries and says, “I still cannot believe she is gone”?
choices: Do not cry because it upsets others
At least she lived a long life
This must be very painful for you
You need to move on now
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the client’s pain is therapeutic and supportive.

questions.question: A client with dementia becomes more confused in the evening. This is best described as:
choices: Neologism
Confabulation
Sundowning
Echolalia
questions.explanation: Worsening confusion later in the day is commonly called sundowning.

questions.question: Which intervention is appropriate for a client with bipolar disorder who is in the depressive phase?
choices: Assess suicide risk and encourage structured activity as tolerated
Withhold antidepressant teaching entirely during assessment as the next step
give multiple stimulating group activities all night as the next step
Use rapid speech to match energy level at this time for now as ordered
questions.explanation: Depression in bipolar disorder requires suicide assessment and supportive activity.

questions.question: A client on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should be monitored for which serious condition?
choices: Permanent hearing loss during assessment as the next step at this time
Tardive dyskinesia only within one dose as the next step at this time for now
Diabetic ketoacidosis in all clients at this time for now as ordered during care
Serotonin syndrome if symptoms such as agitation and hyperreflexia occur
questions.explanation: Agitation, hyperreflexia, and autonomic changes may indicate serotonin syndrome.

questions.question: Which nursing action is best for a client who is socially anxious at a group session?
choices: Sit with client initially and offer gradual participation
Force the client to speak first to build confidence
Exclude client from all future groups for now as ordered
Tell client anxiety is imaginary as ordered during care
questions.explanation: Gradual exposure and support help socially anxious clients participate.

questions.question: A client with delirium is attempting to climb out of bed. Which intervention is priority?
choices: Begin long-term psychoanalysis at this time for now as ordered during care in this client
Keep lights off and room isolated for now as ordered during care in this client
give close observation and address possible causes such as hypoxia or infection
Encourage client to walk alone during care in this client right away at this stage
questions.explanation: Delirium is often due to an underlying medical cause and requires safety plus urgent evaluation.

questions.question: Which statement by a family member of a client with major depression indicates need for further teaching?
choices: I should encourage treatment adherence and follow-up
I should tell him to snap out of it if he wants to improve
I should help reduce isolation when possible during care
I should take suicidal statements seriously in this client
questions.explanation: Minimizing depression is not therapeutic; support and treatment are important.

questions.question: A nurse observes a client repeatedly checking the lock for 30 minutes. The best initial response is:
choices: The door is fine, so your feelings do not matter as ordered
Stop that at once or you will lose privileges during care
What thoughts are making it hard to stop checking right now?
You are wasting everyone’s time right away at this stage in this situation
questions.explanation: Exploring the anxiety behind the behavior is more therapeutic than shaming.

questions.question: A client receiving electroconvulsive therapy should be told that the procedure is commonly used when:
choices: A client wants help memorizing school facts during care in this client right away
Any client with insomnia asks for it in this client right away at this stage
Severe depression does not respond adequately and rapid improvement is needed
